issues.title: [Refactor] diffusion/bcg: Share graph-pool output management
issues.body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #46659 and #46660. The graph-pool allocation and replay copy logic is repeated across attention wrappers and model-specific breaks. These should share output management without forcing different attention implementations through the same compute path.

## Modifications

- Add an optional `output_factory` to `eager_on_graph`: allocate outputs before ending the captured segment, retain weak references, and validate layouts before replay writeback.
- Allow direct writes through `pass_output=True`, preserving H3 embedding's buffer reuse without copying those tensors into themselves.
- Migrate common diffusion attention, H3/VDN attention, H3 embedding, and Qwen Image 2.1 prefix attention. Ordinary eager execution bypasses the factory and extra copies. Existing calls without a factory retain their current behavior.
- Avoid querying the Ulysses group when USP output prediction does not need SP. Update the BCG documentation.

Production code: 115 lines added, 97 removed across five files. Attention algorithms and backend selection are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on one H200 with PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 / CUDA 13.0 at `66de1dcb7a5e7ec9781f66dd751cffbd085182f5`:

- SRT BCG basic/copy/break-helper, diffusion attention outputs, and LTX tests: **35 passed, 33 subtests passed**.
- Qwen Image 2.1 CPU/CUDA, H3 DiT contract, and VDN suites: **181 passed**. Includes exact padded-prefix replay and direct embedding-buffer checks.
- Small real H3 attention modules with random weights: dense SDPA, VDN full-cover, and VDN partial-window branches each captured two segments and matched eager for five changed-input replays at `rtol=0, atol=0`.
- The standalone LTX USP BCG test fails on the base commit without an initialized SP group and passes with this fix.
- Pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed.

Full-checkpoint generation, multi-GPU TP/SP, and AMD/XPU have not been validated in this follow-up.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Bounded Qwen prefix-attention microbenchmark, **not full-model E2E**: one H200, BF16, batch 1, 16 heads x 64, SDPA, 128 padded prefix rows, K/V length Q+384. Measures attention plus one output addition. 20 warmups, then median of 9 batches x 200 calls, synchronized on CUDA. Compared against `c43abd6d9e38a14e81bdb77c648a06353e1c10ee`; execution order was new, base, new repeat.

| Q rows | Mode | Base (us) | New, two runs (us) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 256 | eager | 48.90 | 38.16 / 39.10 |
| 256 | BCG | 82.40 | 80.54 / 81.48 |
| 2048 | eager | 75.45 | 71.83 / 72.00 |
| 2048 | BCG | 97.35 | 96.27 / 96.93 |

Output hashes match across commits. Incremental peak PyTorch allocation is unchanged for BCG and lower for eager in both shapes. BCG performance is effectively neutral; eager avoids an unnecessary allocation/copy. No end-to-end speedup is claimed.

## Checklist

- [x] Run pre-commit.
- [x] Add focused regression tests.
- [x] Update documentation.
- [x] Report correctness and performance evidence with validation limits.
- [x] Follow the existing code style.

issues.title: [Refactor] diffusion: Write MiniMax-H3 and Qwen-Image 2.1 break outputs into caller-allocated buffers
issues.body:
- Four graph breaks in the diffusion breakable CUDA graph now write into outputs the caller allocates right before the break and return nothing: the MiniMax-H3 attention core, the VDN-H3 hybrid attention core, `MiniMaxH3DiTModel._embed`, and Qwen-Image 2.1's `attend_past_prefix_pad`. The captured segment after each break reads those outputs. Before, each break returned fresh tensors on every replay and the graph wrapper copied them into the ones it had captured.
- The caller sizes each output from inputs it already has. The attention outputs take q's shape with v's head dim. The VDN linear readout covers the video rows on a single rank, all local rows under Ulysses, and is absent when the window covers the whole sequence. `forward` allocates the embeddings and the timestep embedding it passes to `_embed`. Each break asserts that its result has the predicted shape and dtype before it copies, since `copy_` would broadcast or cast a misprediction silently.
- The two attention cores go through their breaks only while a breakable graph is being captured; eager runs call the core directly, as before.
- Declared differences:
  - `_embed` takes `embeddings` and `t_emb` and returns `None`. The ComfyUI worker patch in `apps/comfyui_worker_patches/h3.py` still unpacks the old return, but its source-hash check already rejects the current `minimax_h3.py`, so the patch does not install today.
  - `_embed` copies the timestep embedding (`[M, time_embed_dim]`, fp32) into `t_emb` on every forward.
  - A Qwen-Image 2.1 forward that carries a prefix pad but runs eager (the warmups before capture, or a signature without a graph) copies the target attention output once more per layer.
  - VDN-H3 and VSA-H3 reject the breakable graph at startup, so their paths through these breaks run only for direct model callers.
- A unit test captures the Qwen-Image 2.1 prefix-pad break and checks that a replay with a new pad writes the captured output.

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion model: Accelerate conditioning hashing with GPU BLAKE3
issues.body:
## Motivation

This PR follows up on [#46028](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46028), extending the GPU hash optimization introduced for Cosmos3 to other diffusion models with suitable conditioning workloads.

Profiling shows that hashing large visual conditioning tensors adds substantial device-to-host transfers and CPU SHA-256 work before VAE or vision encoding. Reusing the existing GPU [BLAKE3](https://github.com/BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3) implementation keeps tensor-content hashing on the GPU and returns only the 32-byte digest to the CPU.

## Modifications

- Add `use_gpu_conditioning_hash()` to select GPU hashing within an existing conditioning-cache scope. CPU tensors use the original digest, and nested scopes restore the previous policy on exit, including exceptions.
- Reuse `gpu_tensor_blake3` from `python/sglang/kernels/ops/memory/gpu_tensor_hash_blake3.py`. Keep `_fingerprint`'s signature and container recursion; select the digest only in its Tensor branch.
- Enable the policy at these conditioning paths:

| Path | Models |
| --- | --- |
| Ref2VA VAE and vision-encoder inputs | MiniMax-H3, FastH3-Omni |
| Control/reference-video VAE inputs | Cosmos3 Transfer, Cosmos3 multiview and Simulation, Wan2.2-Animate-2 including Distilled |
| Multiple reference images | FLUX.2/Klein and Qwen-Image-Edit through the shared image-VAE stage; Qwen-Image-2.1 VAE and vision encoding; GLM-Image VAE |
| Video-clip memory VAE inputs | JoyAI-Echo |

**Workload selection matters.** The shared `ImageVAEEncodingStage` opts in only when `num_frames == 1 and len(images) > 1`. These are multiple reference images without padded zero frames; images are still hashed and encoded individually. Ordinary I2V inputs contain one image followed by zero frames, and the original digest already filters nonzero blocks on the GPU to avoid transferring the padding. Single-image requests keep the default policy in this stage.

The scoped policy can be reused at other conditioning-cache call sites. Further single-image or model-specific adoption should be based on the actual tensor size, sparsity, and measured hash cost.

## Accuracy Tests

- All 11 completed comparisons for newly adapted workloads produced **bitwise-identical decoded RGB frames and audio samples where present**. The existing Cosmos3 V2V reference comparison also passed.
- GPU digests matched the standard CPU BLAKE3 implementation for the tested conditioning tensors.
- Current cache, model-boundary, and text-encoding regressions: **130 passed, 1 skipped**. Coverage includes CPU fallback, content changes, nested scopes, exception restoration, and posterior sampling/RNG. Pre-commit passed.
- Full-model validation remains pending for JoyAI-Echo, Qwen-Image-Edit-2511, Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo, and GLM-Image. They are integrated but excluded from the performance table below.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition 96GB; Xeon Platinum 8480+ with 16 logical CPUs; SGLang Docker `b1259f3ea327`.

Each mode runs in a separate process on the same GPU: one complete warmup followed by one measured request, using different visual inputs and prompts to avoid warmup cache hits. The baseline retains the original digest, including GPU zero-block filtering; other settings are identical within each pair.

Hash timing includes tensor-content hashing and required transfers with inputs ready, and excludes VAE encoding and upstream waits. E2E includes generation and output saving, excluding model loading. Speedup is original time divided by GPU-hash time.

Outputs: MiniMax/FastH3 896×512, 107 frames; Wan-Animate 576×1024 with a requested 37-frame clip; Cosmos3 832×480, 45 frames per view; Klein 1024×1024. MiniMax uses layerwise offload with 20 DiT layers resident; FastH3 uses Torch SDPA on SM120.

| Workload | Original hash (ms) | GPU hash (ms) | Hash speedup | Original E2E (s) | GPU-hash E2E (s) | E2E speedup | Original hash / E2E |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MiniMax-H3: video, 50 steps | 1743.327 | 23.729 | 73.47× | 930.811 | 937.821 | 0.993× | 0.187% |
| MiniMax-H3: image, 50 steps | 306.479 | 21.549 | 14.22× | 403.547 | 421.576 | 0.957× | 0.076% |

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Hash large conditioning-cache keys in parallel chunks
issues.body:
## Motivation

The conditioning cache keys every encoder call by a SHA-256 of its inputs, and computes the key before it knows whether the call will hit. For an image-conditioned request every key misses on new inputs, so hashing is pure request-path cost. One Qwen-Image-2.1 edit with a 1024x704 reference (resized to 1248x864) hashes three copies of the image:

| key | bytes | time, before |
|---|---|---|
| VAE input (`AutoencoderKLQwenImage21.encode`, after a GPU→CPU copy) | 8.6 MB | 10.1 ms |
| text encoder outer key (the resized PIL image) | 4.3 MB | 3.6 ms |
| vision tower (`_get_flat_visual_features`, processor output after a GPU→CPU copy) | 25.9 MB | 19.9 ms |

(1xH200, server timings around each key.) These run on the host before the vision tower is launched, while the GPU has only the VAE encode to do, so they add almost one to one to the request. Single-threaded `hashlib.sha256` runs at about 1.45 GB/s on the host CPU.

The cache is kept. It is exact, and it serves repeated inputs: the same reference with a new prompt reuses the VAE latents and the vision features, and the same request with a new seed skips the encoders. Only the key gets cheaper.

## Modifications

`runtime/cache/conditioning.py`: `_digest` hashes a buffer of at most 2 MiB with SHA-256 as before. A larger buffer is hashed as SHA-256 over its length and the SHA-256 digests of its 2 MiB chunks. The chunks are hashed on a module-level thread pool of up to eight threads; `hashlib` releases the GIL while it hashes. The digest still covers every byte and keeps SHA-256's collision resistance. Tensors (dense and sparse block paths), PIL images and NumPy arrays use it.

Measured on one host core vs eight threads: a 25 MB buffer takes 16.9 ms with one SHA-256 and 2.3 ms chunked.

Tests: `test_conditioning_cache.py::test_chunked_input_digest_covers_every_byte` sends inputs larger than a chunk through the real cache (a VAE encode and a PIL image key): an equal copy hits; a change in the first byte, at a chunk boundary, in the last element, or in the length misses.

## Accuracy Tests

Keys change format, values do not: a hit returns the stored output as before, and a miss computes it as before.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen-Image-2.1 edit 1024 with the harness's request (distinct inputs per request, so every key misses), measured inside one server that switches between chunked and single-threaded hashing request by request (interleaved rounds; an A/A pair in the same rotation stays within 5 ms):

| | single-threaded keys | this PR | difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1xH200, 8 rounds | 5.177 s | 5.155 s | −22 ms |
| 1xB300, 6 rounds | 2.624 s | 2.603 s | −17 ms |

With this PR, turning the whole conditioning cache off saves only another 13 ms on H200 (it was 39 ms on main), which is what repeated-input users now pay for their hits.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

issues.title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: add a Triton dense attention prefill path for gfx1151
issues.body:
## Motivation

`SDPAImpl.forward` transposes the token-major q/k/v to head-major and hands SDPA a
**non-contiguous** view. On gfx1151 that view costs AOTriton a lot: the same
`attn_fwd` kernel runs at 12.4 / 6.7 / 2.06 TF for 4096 / 8192 / 16384 tokens,
versus 12.4 → 18 TF when the operands are dense. Even the dense number leaves
throughput on the table: a plain Triton prefill kernel reaches 31.8 TF at the
same shape, which is the bulk of diffusion prefill cost.

## What this adds

* `python/sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/attention/flash_attn_dense_triton.py` — a
  non-causal MHA prefill kernel for dense `[B, H, S, D]` operands. It needs no
  masks in the main loop (query length is a multiple of the tile, padding rows of
  K/V are zeroed and their mass is subtracted from the denominator), loads K
  pre-transposed through its strides, and runs `BLOCK_M = BLOCK_N = 64` with 4
  warps and a single pipeline stage. bf16 in, fp32 accumulate, bf16 out; softmax
  keeps the reference's rounding (unscaled q into the WMMA,
  `1/sqrt(D) * log2(e)` on the fp32 scores).
* A gated fast path in `SDPAImpl.forward`: HIP only, `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_TRITON_DENSE_ATTN`
  (default off), bf16, batch 1, equal q/k/v lengths, `head_dim == 128`,
  `seq_len % 64 == 0`, `seq_len >= 4096`, non-causal, no dropout. Everything
  else falls through to the existing SDPA call untouched. Operands are
  materialised head-major once before the kernel sees them; below 4096 tokens
  those copies cost more than the kernel saves, so shorter sequences stay on
  SDPA.

## Numbers (Ryzen AI MAX 395, gfx1151, torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.4, B=1 H=32 D=128 bf16)

Same dense head-major operands for both, kernel-only (median of 10, 3 warmups):

| seq | AOTriton SDPA | Triton | speedup | Triton TF |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 16.4 ms | 9.7 ms | 1.70x | 28.5 |
| 16384 | 239.3 ms | 138.5 ms | 1.73x | 31.8 |

The 16384 row uses the shipped one-stage pipeline; the 4096 row predates the
stage sweep and is unaffected by it.

What the flag actually changes end to end, i.e. including the layout
materialisation the kernel needs versus the strided call the backend makes today:

| seq | today (SDPA on the view) | with this PR | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 22.2 ms | 16.6 ms | 1.34x |
| 8192 | 163.6 ms | 54.3 ms | 3.01x |
| 16384 | 2131 ms | 183.3 ms | 11.6x |

The 16K row is the interesting one: AOTriton's strided-operand regression grows
faster than the work does, so at 128 head dim the gap widens with sequence
length. Diffusion DiT self-attention at 2048x2048 sits exactly there.

## Kernel resources and scaling

Compiled at S=16384 the kernel uses 256 VGPR per lane (the RDNA3 limit) with
**zero spills** and 16 KiB of LDS, which keeps four CTAs resident per CU. A
second pipeline stage doubles LDS to 32 KiB, halves residency, and measured
146.3 ms instead of 138.5 ms — that is why the shipped configuration uses one
stage. Of 81 swept `BLOCK_M x BLOCK_N x warps x stages` points, 66 compiled and
this one ranked first; `BLOCK_M = 128` with 2-4 warps spills 350-1149 registers
and drops to 3.8-6.7 TF.

Sweeping the sequence length shows where the materialisation stops paying:

| seq | SDPA on the view | this PR | speedup | kernel vs dense AOTriton |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1.37 ms | 2.10 ms | 0.65x | 1.81x |
| 2048 | 5.39 ms | 5.58 ms | 0.97x | 1.78x |
| 4096 | 21.7 ms | 16.9 ms | 1.29x | 1.70x |
| 8192 | 150.2 ms | 54.2 ms | 2.77x | 1.62x |
| 16384 | 2180.5 ms | 182.4 ms | 11.95x | 1.64x |
| 32768 | 12932.8 ms | 658.6 ms | 19.64x | 1.65x |

The kernel alone wins at every length (1.62-1.81x against dense AOTriton, and
2.1x to 22x against the strided view); what crosses over is the three
materialisations, which are 69% of the call at 1024 tokens and 20% at 16384.
Hence the 4096-token floor.

Numerics against an fp32 reference: max abs diff 1.1e-3, mean 1.9e-5, no element
above 0.05 (bf16 rounding on both sides).

## Tests

* `test/registered/unit/attention/test_sdpa_triton_dense_attention.py` (CPU, no GPU
  needed; the kernel is mocked): env gate, non-ROCm, torch.compile, causal,
  dropout, fp32, `head_dim != 128`, `seq % 64`, short sequences (`seq < 4096`),
  mismatched lengths, kernel refusal → SDPA fallback; operand strides and `scale`
  forwarded to the kernel. `10 passed`.
* `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_flash_attn_dense_triton.py` (AMD CI):
  fp32-reference numerics at 128/256/512 tokens, zero-padded K/V with `kv_pad`,
  predicate rejections. `4 passed` on gfx1151.

Both were run on gfx1151 with `PYTHONPATH` pointed at a patched copy of the
installed package, so they are not compile-only checks.

## Relation to other work

* #46065 materialises dense SDPA operands; that closes the "strided view" half of
  the gap (AOTriton back to 240 ms at 16K) but not the remaining 1.63x.
* Model-side qkv changes and sparse-attention kernels are out of scope here.

## Caveats

- The default is off: only gfx1151 has been measured. gfx11 should behave the
  same, gfx9x untested — flip the default once there are numbers.
- Sequences below 4096 tokens deliberately stay on SDPA. The floor is the
  measured crossover from the table above, not a derived bound: the kernel alone
  is faster at every length, but the three head-major materialisations dominate
  short calls and make the full path a net loss there.
- End-to-end diffusion (Qwen-Image 2.1 at 2048x2048) throughput is not measured
  in this PR; the benchmark above is operator-level.

issues.title: [Feat] [NPU] qwen-image: Adapt Qwen-Image 2.1 on Ascend
issues.body: Part of #43519 (roadmap item: *Qwen-Image-2.1 — adapt the existing SGLang Diffusion pipeline for Ascend*). ## Motivation Qwen-Image 2.1 already runs on Ascend through `torch_npu`, but two hot paths in the DiT stay on the slow eager implementations: `QwenImage21Attention` forces the native fp32 QK RMSNorm on every platform, and the complex RoPE goes through the complex64 multiply path. This PR routes both to the CANN operators exposed by `torch_npu`: - `torch_npu.npu_rms_norm` for `norm_q` / `norm_k`. - `torch_npu.npu_rotary_mul(..., rotary_mode="interleave")` for the complex RoPE, with the cos/sin tables prepared once per layout and cached. Cos/sin for `npu_rotary_mul` must be expanded with `repeat_interleave(2)`; a plain `cat((c, c), -1)` pairs the wrong frequencies. The previously attempted Triton fast-path enablement on NPU is **not** part of this change: the QK-norm+RoPE Triton kernel is not bit-exact for sequence lengths ≥ 1024 and is 60–95× slower than the eager chain on Ascend. The three kernel files touched by that attempt are restored to their pre-enablement state. issues.title: [Fix] [AMD] diffusion: materialize SDPA operands for long sequences
issues.body:
## Motivation

`SDPAImpl.forward` transposes the `[B, S, H, D]` activations into the `[B, H, S, D]` layout `scaled_dot_product_attention` expects. That transpose is always a strided view, and AOTriton's flash path only applies to **dense** operands, so on HIP a long-sequence attention silently falls back to a generic kernel.

Measured on gfx1151 (AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, 32 heads x 128, bf16, one SDPA call):

| S | strided | dense | gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1.39 ms | 1.18 ms | 1.18x |
| 2048 | 4.75 ms | 4.35 ms | 1.09x |
| 4096 | 20.84 ms | 15.99 ms | 1.30x |
| 8192 | 184.2 ms | 61.2 ms | 3.01x |
| 16384 | 2255 ms | 242.9 ms | **9.28x** |

The cliff is at S=8192: below it the strided layout still reaches the flash kernel (13-15 TFLOPS), above it drops to 2 TFLOPS while the dense operands hold 18 TFLOPS.

## Modifications

- Extract `sdpa_operands()` from `SDPAImpl.forward`. It still returns the heads-first view, and on HIP it materializes the operands **when `S >= 8192`**.
- The copy is layout-only: values are bit-identical, so there is no accuracy change.
- Below the threshold nothing changes. Qwen-Image 2.1 at 1024^2 (S=4096) is 5.7% *slower* when the copy is unconditional, because the per-layer allocation costs more than the 1.3x kernel gain - so the gate is a sequence threshold, not just a device check.
- The common path (CUDA, and short sequences on any device) keeps the zero-copy view and is the first branch.

## Accuracy Tests

- `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_sdpa_operand_layout.py` (new, runs in the `diffusion-unit-1-gpu-h100` suite): heads-first layout and values; short sequences keep the zero-copy view; long sequences are dense only on HIP; the copy preserves every bit (`torch.equal` against the transposed view).
- End to end, the change only moves tensor layout, so no numerical change is expected by construction. Verified on Qwen-Image 2.1 at 1024^2 and 2048^2 with a fixed seed: identical image, no metric shift.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen-Image 2.1, default environment, `torch_sdpa` backend, gfx1151. Seconds per denoising step (mean over all steps), two runs per arm:

| Shape | before | after | gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024^2 / 20 steps | 3.8524 | 3.8523 | 1.00x |
| 2048^2 / 12 steps | 78.04 / 77.42 | 22.04 / 22.11 | **3.54x** |

Within-arm spread <1%. The 2048^2 gain is AOTriton flash instead of the generic kernel; the 1024^2 row confirms the threshold leaves short sequences untouched.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit (`isort` + `ruff` pass).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations (no user-facing docs describe this backend detail).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

issues.body:
Motivation

Qwen-Image 2.1's FFN activation fast path (fused_silu_mul_bitexact) is gated on current_platform.is_cuda(). On ROCm that predicate is False (PlatformEnum.ROCM), so the optimization is dead code on AMD hardware — even though the fused kernel is plain Triton (no CUDA JIT / PTX) and reproduces the eager silu(a) * b chain bit-exactly on HIP.

This is the same situation the XPU port fixed in #41940, which enabled the identical kernel via (x.is_cuda or x.is_xpu). This PR does the equivalent for ROCm/HIP.

Modifications

python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/qwen_image21.py:

  • Add _silu_mul_device = current_platform.is_cuda() or current_platform.is_hip().

  • Gate QwenImage21FeedForward.forward on _silu_mul_device instead of the vendor-pure _is_cuda.

Every other fast path in the module (RoPE, QK-norm, packed QKV, SDPA) stays CUDA-only, because those really are CUDA JIT / PTX kernels. The existing BitExactFusionGate still self-verifies the first call and permanently disables the path on any mismatch, so a platform that turns out not to be bit-exact falls back to eager instead of diverging.

python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_qwen_image21_silu_mul_fusion.py (new):

  • assert the guard tracks the CUDA-like device family;

  • assert fused_silu_mul_bitexact is bit-exact vs F.silu(a) * b at the FFN activation shapes.

Accuracy Tests

Environment: AMD Ryzen AI MAX 395 (Strix Halo), Radeon 8060S Graphics, gfx1151 (RDNA 3.5), torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.4 (hip 7.2.53211), SGLang Diffusion, attention backend torch_sdpa.

issues.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #46429. `resolve_sequential_cfg` decides between packed and sequential CFG from each rank's own free memory ([L159](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5971f47bc8eacd8989cb6dd67e46b4fc6dbec2ad/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/flux3_image.py#L159)). The two paths issue different TP all-reduces and SP exchanges per step, so when the ranks decide differently their collectives no longer match, and the request hangs or fails (details in the issue).

## Modifications

- Take the MIN of free memory over the TP and SP groups before comparing, as `_cache_fits` already does in the Qwen-Image 2.1 stage ([L351-L358](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/5971f47bc8eacd8989cb6dd67e46b4fc6dbec2ad/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/pipelines_core/stages/model_specific_stages/qwen_image21.py#L351-L358)).
- New test `test_sequential_cfg_is_agreed_across_ranks` in `test_flux3_image_stages.py` runs two CPU ranks, once as TP=2 and once as Ulysses SP=2, with rank 1 reporting 1 MiB free, and checks that both ranks choose sequential CFG. On main both subtests fail with `AssertionError: [False, True]`; with this change the file passes.

## Accuracy Tests

2x H200, `black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-base` (base e262b44), TP=2, 2048x2048, 20 steps, with another process holding memory on GPU 1 only so that the ranks would split. Without this change the request got no response for 300 s; with it, both ranks chose sequential CFG and the request completed. Two runs with the change gave bit-identical images, and they are also bit-identical to the output without the change when memory is held on both GPUs, so that both ranks take the sequential path.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not measured. The change adds at most two CPU all-reduces of one int64 per denoise call, before the step loop.

issues.body:
## Summary

Extend the exact RGB preprocessing introduced in #45398 beyond Cosmos3, using one shared resize/crop/normalize entry point rather than per-model kernels.

This PR includes the original commit from @xupinjie with its authorship preserved because #45398 is still open. It should land after that PR; merging main afterwards will remove the overlapping diff.

- Cover FLUX.2/Klein reference images, Qwen-Image-Edit 2509/2511 VAE inputs, Wan TI2V, Cosmos3 I2V/V2V, and RGB conversion in the shared image-VAE stage.
- Upload compact uint8 pixels, fuse Lanczos/crop/FP32 normalization, and fast-path identity resize. Preserve Pillow rounding, each model's crop geometry, and encoder input strides.
- Bound video decoding for first-frame and control-video consumers instead of decoding the full clip and slicing afterwards.
- Retain CPU processing for unsupported platforms/modes and small workloads; reuse `SGLANG_FORCE_CPU_IMAGE_PREPROCESSING=1` as an override. Include output area when deciding whether an upscale is too small for GPU processing.
- Document temporary VRAM, first-use compilation, and the distinction between input-chain and full-request speedups.

The extension beyond #45398 adds about 146 production lines and removes 30, with no additional production files.

## Accuracy And Tests

- Registered CUDA entry points: all 5 kernel tests and all 3 runtime preprocessing tests pass.
- Existing input-validation/Cosmos3 suite: **158 passed, 55 subtests passed**.
- Exact external Diffusers FLUX.2 and Qwen VAE processor comparisons, including odd/portrait/4K shapes; compare both values (`rtol=atol=0`) and strides.
- Real Wan TI2V geometry and real MP4 first/last/prefix decoding match the CPU reference exactly. Non-RGB floating-point VAE inputs retain their original normalization policy.
- Native E2E: all **12 paired output files** (warmup plus three distinct requests for each of three models) match baseline SHA-256, including saved PNG/MP4 files. No GT or consistency threshold changes.
- Pre-commit and diff whitespace checks pass.

Cosmos3 is covered by preprocessing tests, not a full checkpoint E2E run. No general cross-hardware bitwise-equivalence claim is made.

## Performance

Hardware/software: **1 NVIDIA H200, 143771 MiB reported total VRAM**, Intel Xeon Platinum 8558P host; PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Triton 3.8.0, Diffusers 0.37.0, Transformers 5.19.0, Pillow 11.3.0, PyAV 16.1.0.

### Complete Native Requests

Baseline: `5f62e23d3051d09fa711f825b20abead20c3a717`; candidate: `17c917344bd639a90abae9c2644c12de96853396`. Both sides use the native SGLang pipeline, one GPU, batch 1, four steps, seed 42, `quality=exact`, manual/resident placement, no torch.compile or CUDA Graph. Input: distinct 1920x1080 PNGs/prompts to avoid conditioning-cache hits. One warmup and three measured requests per process; report medians, excluding loading but **including file decoding, preprocessing, transfer, learned encoding, denoising, decoding, output encoding/saving, and API return**.

| Model / Output | Baseline | GPU input path | Observed latency reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| FLUX.2-klein-4B / 512x512 | 494.3 ms | 454.6 ms | 8.0% |
| Wan2.2-TI2V-5B / 17x704x1248 | 2240.9 ms | 2210.4 ms | 1.4% |
| Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 / 512x512 | 1530.7 ms | 1498.9 ms | 2.1% |

These are bounded low-step samples, not a statistical guarantee or a universal model speedup. Longer denoising workloads amortize input processing further.

Peak allocated VRAM (same requests): FLUX 16893.02 -> 16904.59 MiB; Wan 48772.43 -> 48772.53 MiB; Qwen 57158.03 -> 57170.23 MiB. This is **not zero-extra-VRAM**: temporary pixels and coefficient buffers live on GPU. Peak reserved VRAM was unchanged for Wan/Qwen and increased by 12 MiB for FLUX.

### Input Chain In Isolation

Synthetic RGB JPEGs, quality 92, warm filesystem cache, resize to 1024x1024, three warmups plus ten measured samples. Includes JPEG file decode, resize/crop/normalize, H2D, and CUDA synchronization; excludes learned encoder/denoiser work. CPU override vs GPU path in the same checkout; outputs match exactly.

| Source | CPU input chain | GPU input chain |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1024x1024 | 22.94 ms | 12.55 ms |
| 1920x1080 | 60.97 ms | 25.22 ms |
| 3840x2160 | 204.44 ms | 112.20 ms |

Image/video codec decoding and tokenization remain on CPU where they were previously. Output codecs are unchanged: this does not silently substitute NVENC for libx264 or claim that all CPU work has moved to GPU.

## Motivation

Qwen-Image 2.1 FP8 inference repeats activation quantization for sibling projections and materializes intermediate BF16 tensors before quantization.

This PR reduces that overhead through shared-input quantization and two fused Triton kernels. Together, these optimizations reduced end-to-end latency by 3.96% on the tested RTX 4090 D workload.

## Modifications
- Share dynamic FP8 input quantization across Q/K/V and gate/up projections while retaining the original separate GEMMs.
- Fuse SiLU + multiplication + dynamic FP8 quantization before the MLP down projection.
- Fuse LayerNorm + modulation + dynamic FP8 quantization before image QKV and gate/up projections.
- Preserve intermediate BF16 rounding and use direct FP32-to-E4M3 conversion to avoid double rounding on SM89.
- Verify the norm and SiLU fusion paths against the existing implementation on first use, falling back on mismatch.
- Extract a shared ATen-compatible Welford reduction for the existing modulation kernel and the new norm/FP8 kernel.
- Share FP8 projection eligibility checks and use explicit forward branches instead of temporary keyword-argument dictionaries.
- Add numerical tests, runtime fallback coverage, and manual microbenchmarks.

The new kernels live under sglang.kernels.ops.activation and sglang.kernels.ops.layernorm.

Runtime dispatch is restricted to supported SM89, TP1, eager dynamic FP8 configurations. The two producer fusions initially target the measured [1, 4096, 4096] image-token shape used for 1024×1024 generation. Unsupported configurations retain the existing path.


## Accuracy Tests

Tested Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo on one RTX 4090 D with 1024×1024 generation, eight steps, seed 42, and a fixed text prompt.

This demonstrates bit-exact output on the tested workload. 

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Configuration: RTX 4090 D, one GPU, Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo, 1024×1024, eight steps, seed 42, TP1 eager execution, FP8 transformer and text encoder, conditioning cache disabled.

### Kernel performance

| Optimization | Before | After | Latency reduction | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Shared-input FP8 quantization | Separate quantization per projection | One quantization per group | Not measured separately | — |
| SiLU + mul + FP8 quantization | 0.569 ms | 0.273 ms | 52.0% | 2.08× |
| LayerNorm + modulation + FP8 quantization | 0.0832 ms | 0.0440 ms | 47.1% | 1.89× |

### Incremental end-to-end performance

Each row measures the benefit of adding that optimization to the preceding implementation.

| Optimization added | Before | After | Latency reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Shared-input FP8 quantization | ~2.734 s | ~2.690 s | ~1.6% |
| SiLU + mul + FP8 quantization | 2.686 s | 2.618 s | 2.54% |
| LayerNorm + modulation + FP8 quantization | 2.866 s | 2.841 s | 0.85% |

### Combined end-to-end performance

Both paths use the same configuration, including unchanged upstream text_encoder=layerwise-offload. The baseline disables all three additions while retaining existing upstream optimizations.

| Metric | All three disabled | All three enabled | Latency reduction | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| End-to-end | 2.957 s | 2.840 s | 3.96% | 1.041× |
| Denoising | 2.472 s | 2.354 s | 4.76% | 1.050× |

End-to-end measures the synchronized stage span from input validation through decoding, excluding model loading, warmup, queueing, output serialization, and network overhead.

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Remove per-step host syncs and uploads in video models
issues.body:
Depends on #46045 (host-sync guards in `test/unit/host_sync_guard.py`); this branch is stacked on it.

## Motivation

Video pipelines run long denoising loops where every blocking host read or pageable upload stalls the host on the previous step's kernels, and several of them rebuilt request-constant RoPE tables or masks on every forward. This PR removes those per-step costs model by model. Outputs are bitwise unchanged.

## Modifications

- **MOVA** (`model_specific_stages/mova.py`, `bridges/mova_dual_tower.py`): the loop uploaded both timesteps every step and `step_from_to` read them back with `float()`, four syncs per step. The paired schedule is uploaded once and the scheduler steps on the host values. Every forward re-uploaded both towers' CPU complex128 RoPE tables (six blocking copies, ~17 MB for audio) and redid the full-sequence concats, and every bridge layer rebuilt its fp32 cos/sin caches (30 layers x 2 directions); tables and bridge caches are built once per request and freed when the loop ends.
- **MiniMax-H3 / FastH3** (`dits/minimax_h3.py`, `minimax_h3_adaln_cache.py`): FastH3 PDD heads copied that step's weight and bias from the host stacks, four blocking copies per step; the stacks are uploaded once per (device, dtype) and indexed by step. The AdaLN online cache indexed its slabs with a 0-dim device slot (a host read, two per step); it now gathers with `index_select` and keeps the old strides.
- **HunyuanVideo** (`dits/hunyuanvideo.py`): the forward built the RoPE cos/sin on the host and copied both to the device every forward (~59 MB per step at 720p x 125 frames). The uploaded tables are kept per request in an underscore `Req.extra` key, which the disaggregation transport skips.
- **Helios** (`helios_denoising.py`, `dits/helios.py`): frame indices were built on the host and uploaded by each of four RoPE embeddings per forward (eight syncs per CFG step); they are built on the latent device. Every block cast the full-sequence [B, L, 6, D] modulation to fp32 (~1.4 GB per block at 384x640); the compact rows are cast once before the expand/concat.
- **Wan family** (`dits/causal_wanvideo.py`, `dits/wanvideo.py`): causal Wan (LongLive2) copied its host RoPE tables to the device every forward; they are uploaded once per request and chunk position. Wan and causal Wan blocks each cast the batch-wide modulation to fp32; the forward casts it once (the per-token TI2V table keeps its fused bf16 path).
- **LTX-2** (`dits/ltx_2.py`, `ltx_2/denoising.py`; paths not touched by #45966): `prepare_video_coords` uploaded two constant tensors per call (every forward on the LTX-2.3 one-stage path, every step for JoyEcho memory coords); they are uploaded once per device. HQ res2s: the SDE coefficient NaN replacement went through a 0-dim boolean index (nonzero on get and set, four calls per step) and is now a `torch.where`; the 100-iteration bongmath refinement hoists its fp64 casts and `h * a21`; the stage-1 step size starts from the step's host sigmas instead of `.cpu()` reads.
- **JoyEcho** (`joy_echo/denoising.py`): every DMD step read sigma and sigma_next with `.item()`; the loop takes fp32 host and device copies of the schedule once. With the memory bank (shot >= 2) the shot-constant cross masks, audio block mask and memory RoPE coords are built once per loop instead of every step.
- **SANA-WM / SANA-Video2** (`sana_wm*.py`, `sana_wm/streaming*.py`, `sana_video2.py`): the cache-type flag was uploaded in every block's clean pass and read back by the next chunk (20 uploads + 20 reads per chunk) and is now a host tensor; self-forcing steps read their timestep once per chunk; `forward_long` windows camera/Plucker inputs once per chunk so the UCPE and Plucker caches hit; the UCPE invalid-ray fix is a `torch.where`; the chunked refiner reads its sigmas from a host copy and builds each block's RoPE once on the device. SANA-Video2 builds its RoPE tables once per latent shape instead of uploading complex128 tables twice per forward.
- **Cosmos3 world models** (`dits/cosmos_dreams.py`, `dits/cosmos3_sim_auto.py`, `cosmos3_simulation/sim_auto.py`): Dreams zeroed null-action V slots by indexing with a Python list in each of 36 layers (a blocking upload each); the slots are per-frame slices. Sim-Auto's scatter/gather indexes, mRoPE frame ids and generated-frame masks are built once per chunk on the device. The default Cosmos3 T2V/I2V loop is untouched (#45967 covers its CFG window).

Tests:
- `test_mova_denoising.py`: steps never upload or read device timesteps (`SyncOnRead` schedule, one upload); RoPE tables built once per request; outputs bitwise equal.
- `test_minimax_h3_pdd_offline.py`, `test_minimax_h3_adaln_cache.py`: heads uploaded once; slab gathers run under `forbid_host_syncs` with the old values and strides.
- `test_hunyuanvideo_rope_upload.py`, `test_wan_step_host_overhead.py`: RoPE tables uploaded once per request (per chunk position for causal Wan), identical tables; blocks receive fp32 modulation.
- `test_helios_step_host_overhead.py`: frame indices live on the latent device; blocks receive fp32 modulation.
- `test_ltx2_step_host_overhead.py`: video-coord constants uploaded once; SDE coefficients under `forbid_host_syncs`; the refinement casts once.
- `test_joy_echo_denoising_host_overhead.py`: host/device sigma copies, steps never read device sigmas, the memory prefix is built once.
- `sana_wm/test_host_overhead.py`, `test_sana_video2.py`, `test_cosmos3_simulation_host_overhead.py`, `test_cosmos_dreams.py`, `test_cosmos3_sim_auto.py`: the SANA-WM, SANA-Video2 and Cosmos3 world-model paths above.

No hunk overlaps #45942, #45943, #45944, #45948, #45965, #45966, #45967, #45977, #45978, #45979 or #45987; each of them still applies on top of this branch.

## Accuracy Tests

2xH200, eager profiles, two requests per model with different inputs. Decoded frames (and audio where the model produces it) are bitwise identical to main:

| model (request) | GPUs | outputs compared | main vs PRs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I 1024x1024, 40 steps | 1 | pixels | identical (2/2) |

- **Ideogram-4** (`dits/ideogram.py`, `model_specific_stages/ideogram.py`, `progressive_resolution/ideogram.py`): every forward cast the (B, T+I, 53248) fp32 LLM features to bf16, masked them and ran the RMSNorm and the 53248 -> 4608 projection (plus its TP all-gather) on inputs that never change within a request. issues.body:
Branch: mick/diffusion-vae-height-gather-host (on main 005333d029), commit 2a864e5c69

## Motivation

Spatial-parallel VAE decode shards the frame height across the decode ranks. Each output gather (`gather_and_trim_height`) and each height-dependent op (the Wan VAE's row-sharded attention, strided convs) first learns every rank's shard height through `gather_height_sizes`. That helper built a one-element CUDA tensor from a Python int, all-gathered it over the device group and read each element back with `.item()`.

Both the pageable H2D copy and the read-back block the host until every kernel queued before them has run. In the middle of a decode, that drains the GPU queue: the GPU idles while the host relaunches the rest of the decoder. The Wan VAE decodes one latent frame per call and pays this twice per frame. A Cosmos3-Nano 189-frame decode on 4xB300 (48 latent frames) issued 96 stream syncs, which held the host for 590 ms in one profiled request. About 420 ms of the 2.47 s decode window was GPU idle.

## Modifications

- `layers/parallel_conv.py`: `gather_height_sizes` all-gathers the heights as a CPU int64 tensor over the group's gloo `cpu_group` instead of the device group. It does no device work and no stream sync. The values and the call order are the same on every rank, so every decode returns the same result.
- `test_vae_spatial_parallel_decode.py`: `test_height_sizes_are_gathered_on_the_host` runs two gloo ranks with uneven shards (3 and 2 rows) and passes `meta` tensors with no device group. The gather returns `[3, 2]` on both ranks. The old device gather cannot run on meta tensors.
- `test_ltx_vae_parallel_decode.py`: the fake decode group now carries a `cpu_group`.

## Accuracy Tests

The heights are integers and only travel over a different group, so every output is bitwise unchanged. Cosmos3-Nano T2V 720p 189 frames on 4xB300: the MP4s are byte-identical to the base (md5 a494ab96ce / 80597a2763 for two requests). They are also identical at x264 crf 0 together with "Encode Cosmos3 video while it decodes".

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Stop the idle loop from starving async-save replies
issues.body:
## Motivation

With `--async-output-save`, single requests got slower and noisier instead of
staying flat. On 1xH200, Z-Image-Turbo went from 0.92 s to 1.00 s median (max
1.27 s) and Qwen-Image-2.1 from 4.45 s to 4.49–4.60 s (max 4.84 s), with almost
no throughput gain on Qwen-Image-2.1.

The finalize thread sends its reply on the ROUTER socket under `_socket_lock`.
While that finalize ran, the idle event loop waited with
`with self._socket_lock: self._poller.poll(timeout=1)` and took the lock straight
back in `recv_reqs()`. The loop held the lock almost all the time, and
`threading.Lock` is not fair (a semaphore on Linux / CPython 3.12): each release
wakes the finalize thread, but the loop re-acquires the lock a few microseconds
later, before the woken thread runs. The reply sat behind that loop for tens to
hundreds of milliseconds.

## Modifications

`Scheduler._wait_idle()` replaces both idle waits (in-flight finalize and the
dynamic-batching delay). With a finalize in flight it waits on the finalize
futures without the socket lock, for at most 1 ms, so new requests are still
picked up as before; with none in flight it polls the socket as before.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerical change: only the scheduler's idle wait changes.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

1xH200, `--model-type diffusion --warmup-mode server --performance-mode speed`,
1024x1024 PNG returned as b64_json. Each arm runs on a fresh server: two 3-step
warmups, then 10 sequential requests with distinct prompts, then 8 requests at
concurrency 2. Arms are interleaved and repeated twice; main is 49a2fbf817.

| case | arm | single median (s) | single max (s) | throughput (req/s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Z-Image-Turbo, 9 steps | main | 0.920 / 0.922 | 0.925 / 0.927 | 1.094 / 1.094 |
| | main + `--async-output-save` | 1.006 / 1.000 | 1.246 / 1.269 | 1.117 / 1.129 |
| | **this PR** + `--async-output-save` | **0.921 / 0.920** | **0.924 / 0.924** | **1.128 / 1.128** |
| Qwen-Image-2.1, 40 steps | main | 4.450 / 4.446 | 4.459 / 4.464 | 0.2261 / 0.2261 |
| | main + `--async-output-save` | 4.490 / 4.604 | 4.569 / 4.838 | 0.2268 / 0.2271 |
| | **this PR** + `--async-output-save` | **4.446 / 4.446** | **4.459 / 4.461** | **0.2279 / 0.2280** |

With this PR, single-request latency under `--async-output-save` matches the
synchronous path, and the flag now gives the throughput it was meant to: +3.1%
on Z-Image and +0.8% on Qwen-Image-2.1 at concurrency 2.

Instrumented run (Qwen-Image-2.1, temporary timestamps around the reply's
`send_multipart`; 10 single requests per arm): the time the finalize thread
waited for `_socket_lock` after finishing the save was 14–51 ms median and up
to 262 ms on main, and 0.00 ms for every request with this PR. The save itself
took ~92 ms on either path. At concurrency 2 the wait was already ~0 on main:
the loop is inside the next forward instead of idling on the lock.

- [x] Existing scheduler unit tests pass on 1xH200 (144 passed, 1 skipped).
- [x] The first new test fails 5/5 against the previous idle wait and passes with this PR.

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Keep shared denoising paths off the host and add host-sync test guards
issues.body:
## Motivation

A denoising step that reads a device value on the host (`item()`, `float(t)`, `if t:`, `nonzero`, boolean-mask indexing) or uploads a constant with a pageable copy blocks the host until the stream drains. The host then cannot queue the next step while the GPU runs this one. These regressions pass every numeric test, so they come back. This PR adds unit-test guards for them and removes the ones in shared code: RoPE position setup, two schedulers, the DMD stage and the ring-attention hop.

The model-specific fixes are in two follow-ups that use these guards: image models (#<B>) and video models (#<C>).

## Modifications

Guards (`test/unit/host_sync_guard.py`):
- `no_cuda_sync(allow=...)` / `assert_no_cuda_sync(fn, ...)` run the code under `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("warn")` plus explicit `synchronize()` calls, and fail with the call site of every sync whose issuing function is not allow-listed. They skip without CUDA and restore the debug mode.
- `SyncOnRead` is a CPU stand-in for device tensors (timesteps, sigmas, masks): host reads of its values raise, and `.cpu()` is the explicit copy that is allowed.
- `forbid_host_syncs()` is a `TorchDispatchMode` that fails on the ops that sync on CUDA whatever tensor they read: scalar reads, `nonzero`, boolean-mask indexing, data-dependent output shapes.
- The contributing guide documents the three.

Shared hot paths:
- `rotary_embedding/mrope.py`: `OneDRotaryEmbedding` keyed an LRU cache on `tuple(pos.tolist())`, a device read per axis plus a hash over thousands of floats, and a pageable upload on a miss. FLUX.1/Kontext/FLUX.2, JoyImage, LingBot and the Wan sequence-shard path paid it per image, text and condition axis on every request. It now computes from the device positions directly (same ops, same values).
- `rotary_embedding/{utils,base}.py`, `layernorm.py`: `apply_qk_norm_rope`, `apply_flashinfer_rope_qk_inplace` and both `RotaryEmbedding` paths rebuilt `[offset, offset + seq)` with an `arange` (and a `repeat` for batch > 1) in every block when the caller passes no positions: 64-120 launches per step in eager mode for FLUX.2, Z-Image, Qwen-Image, Wan and others. `rope_positions()` shares one read-only tensor per shape. Compile and graph capture still build their own, so a capture never fills the cache with an arange it did not execute.
- `schedulers/kandinsky6_piflow.py`: the policy rollout looped `range(substeps.max().item())`, a device read right after the DiT forward on every step (video and audio scheduler). The substep counts now come from a host copy of the same fp32 math.
- `schedulers/scheduling_helios.py`: UniPC built `torch.tensor()` over lists of 0-dim device tensors and uploaded `0.5` constants, about a dozen syncs per step; they are stacked and filled on the device, and `linalg.solve` becomes `linalg.solve_ex` (same kernels, no host-side singularity check). The DMD path read the timestep twice per step through `torch.full(..., tensor)`; it is now cast and expanded on the device.
- `stages/denoising_dmd.py` (Wan DMD / FastWan): `int(t.item())` per step now comes from a host copy of the same schedule, and the per-step NaN assert is OR-ed on the device and checked once after the loop (same message; a NaN request still fails).
- `attention/backends/flash_attn.py`, `attention/layer.py`: the ring hop built `cu_seqlens_q/k` with `torch.tensor(..., device=...)` on every hop of every block, twice per hop for the tail-pad path. The hop now uses the cached `cu_seqlens_on_device`, moved next to the FA backend so the varlen and ring paths share it.

Tests (the fix tests fail on main):
- `test_host_sync_guard.py`: the three guards catch scalar reads, explicit synchronizes, boolean-mask indexing and data-dependent shapes, let device-side selects through, honor the allow list and restore the debug mode.
- `test_denoising_host_sync.py`: one CFG request through the shared `DenoisingStage` loop with `SyncOnRead` timesteps matches a plain run, and runs under `no_cuda_sync` on CUDA; one DMD request with `SyncOnRead` timesteps matches a plain run bitwise, and NaN latents still raise.
- `test_rope_host_sync.py`: `FluxPosEmbed` with `SyncOnRead` positions matches bitwise; positions are built once per shape, rebuilt under compile and capture.
- `test_scheduler_host_sync.py`: PiFlow and Helios UniPC/DMD steps with `SyncOnRead` schedules match plain runs bitwise, NaN bits included.
- `test_attention_host_sync.py`: two ring hops get `[0, n]` int32 bounds from the same device tensors.

No hunk overlaps #45942, #45943, #45944, #45948, #45965, #45966, #45967, #45977, #45978, #45979 or #45987; each of them still applies on top of this branch.

## Accuracy Tests

2xH200, eager. Decoded outputs are bitwise identical to main for every model below, two requests each with different inputs (pixels for images, decoded frames and audio for video), with this PR and both follow-ups applied:

| model (request) | GPUs | outputs compared | main vs PRs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I 1024x1024, 40 steps | 1 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 edit 1024x1024, 40 steps | 1 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Z-Image-Turbo 1024x1024, 9 steps, TP2 | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| FLUX.3 Klein Base 1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Ideogram-4 FP8 1024x1024, 20 steps, TP2 | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2I 1280x720, 35 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | pixels | identical (2/2) |
| Cosmos3-Nano T2V 1280x720x61, 35 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | frames | identical (2/2) |
| HunyuanVideo 848x480x61, 30 steps, Ulysses 2 | 2 | frames | identical (2/2) |
| LTX-2 two-stage 768x512x121, 40 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | frames + audio | identical (2/2) |
| Wan2.2-T2V-A14B 1280x720x33, 40 steps, CFG parallel | 2 | frames | identical (2/2) |
| MiniMax-H3 T2VA 1344x768 4 s, 12 steps, Ulysses 2 | 2 | frames + audio | identical (2/2) |
| MOVA-360p I2VA 640x352x97, 20 steps, TP2 | 2 | frames + audio | identical (2/2) |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Host syncs inside the denoising stage, counted with `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("warn")` around the stage's forward on a real server request (rank 0, second request, per denoising step):

None of the twelve models above runs the code this PR changes in a way that syncs per step: their counts move only through the follow-ups (#<B>, #<C>). The paths changed here are FLUX.1/FLUX.2/JoyImage/LingBot RoPE setup, Kandinsky-6 PiFlow, Helios, Wan DMD / FastWan and ring attention on the FA backend. A GPU sync count and A/B for those (FastWan2.2-TI2V DMD, Wan2.1 with ring degree 2, FLUX.2 klein) is still to be run.

The CUDA guard tests (`no_cuda_sync`) ran on an H200 and pass.

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Write uncompressed PNG responses without Pillow's row filters
issues.body:
## Motivation

Image responses are encoded as PNG with zlib level 0 by default since #45987. Pillow still runs its adaptive row filter at that level: for every row it tries the PNG filters and keeps the one with the smallest sum (the encoded files use filters 1 and 2). At level 0 the deflate stream is stored, not compressed, so the filter cannot make the file smaller. It only costs time, and the time is on the output rank between the end of the forward and the reply:

| frame | Pillow, `compress_level=0` | unfiltered rows in stored blocks |
|---|---|---|
| 1024x1024 RGBA (Qwen-Image-2.1) | 74.9 ms | 4.3 ms |
| 1280x720 RGB (Cosmos3 T2I) | 60.9 ms | 2.8 ms |

(One core of a Xeon Platinum 8558P, `Pillow` 13.0.0, zlib 1.3.2. OpenCV's level-0 encoder takes 37.0 / 26.5 ms.)

## Modifications

`entrypoints/utils.py`: `_encode_image_frame` writes a uint8 frame with `compress_level == 0` itself: unfiltered rows (filter byte 0) in one `zlib.compress(rows, 0)` IDAT, behind the same IHDR Pillow writes. Any other level, and non-uint8 frames, still go through Pillow.

The PNG is the same image:
- The IHDR is byte-identical. Pillow writes no other chunks on this path (no gAMA, sRGB, pHYs or text), so the only difference is how the IDAT data is filtered and split: one IDAT chunk instead of Pillow's 64 KiB chunks.
- Decoded pixels, mode and `info` are equal for gray, gray + alpha, RGB and RGBA frames.
- The file is slightly smaller (1024x1024 RGBA: 4,195,716 bytes instead of 4,196,804).

Tests:
- `test_output_saving.py`: levels None, 0 and 75 no longer call Pillow's save, level 100 still saves through Pillow at `compress_level=9`, and every saved file decodes to the source frame. On main the uncompressed cases call Pillow and fail.
- `test_image_response_bytes.py`: the returned-bytes test also covers two-channel (gray + alpha) frames.

## Accuracy Tests

The decoded pixels are identical to the frame the pipeline produced, so the served image does not change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Client latency (median of 5 after warmup), main vs this PR, a fresh server per arm, distinct inputs per request; the Qwen arms ran in pairs on two GPUs and swapped GPUs between rounds.

1xH200 (Qwen-Image-2.1, `--performance-mode speed`) and 2xH200 (Cosmos3-Nano T2I, CFG parallel):

| Cosmos3-Nano T2I 720p, round 1 / round 2 | 0.909 / 0.911 s | 0.893 / 0.895 s |

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Keep every component resident in auto mode when memory allows
issues.body:
## Motivation

`--performance-mode auto` places components from a static per-model allowlist. Above `keep_resident_min_available_gb` (the model's value, else 45 GB for image and 120 GB for video models) only `keep_resident_components` stay resident: the VAE by default, plus the DiT for image models. Everything else streams layer by layer at any memory size:
- Z-Image, Ideogram-4, FLUX, Qwen-Image and LTX-2 stream their text encoder even on a 288 GB GPU. A B300 server log reads `267.1 GiB of free device memory selects layerwise offload for text_encoder` and then `resident=0/36`; Z-Image-Turbo spends 0.066 s of a 0.354 s request moving 3.4 GB over PCIe.
- Wan2.2-T2V/I2V-A14B list `auto` in `dit_layerwise_offload_modes` and set no threshold, so both 14B experts stream layer by layer on every GPU, including H200/B200/B300. That also pins ~54 GB of host memory per rank.

On H100, Z-Image-Turbo with every component resident was 12% faster than auto (0.701/0.699 vs 0.793/0.799 s). The memory-aware fix was meant to come from the warmup-calibrated planner (#37917/#37918), which is not merged. This PR adds a conservative interim rule.

## Modifications

- Memory-rich tier in auto mode (`ServerArgsAutoTuner._fits_all_components_resident`): when the least-free selected GPU has at least twice the per-GPU weight bytes free, every component without an explicit placement stays resident. That means no default layerwise list, no DiT layerwise and component offload cleared, which is the placement `speed` mode gives. Explicit placement flags still win per component.
  - Weights are sized before load from the cached checkpoint's safetensors headers (`checkpoint_component_sizes` in `loader/utils.py`): every `model_index.json` component, counted in its serving precision (`resolve_component_precision`, else as stored), with DiT folders divided by `tp_size`. Text encoders count as full copies even when TP-folded, which is conservative.
  - The tier does not apply, and the per-model policy runs as before, when the checkpoint is not fully cached yet, holds non-safetensors or quantized weights, or is overridden (`--quantization`, `--transformer-weights-path`, SVDQuant, component paths, weights or quantizations, model overlays). It also does not apply with dynamic batching (the factor of two assumes one request's activations), on shared host/device memory (GB10) or on MPS.
  - The rule is platform-agnostic. On ROCm, where auto has no layerwise defaults and offloads the text encoder whole, a GPU that fits the rule now keeps it resident too.
- Wan2.2-T2V/I2V-A14B set `keep_resident_min_available_gb=120` with the DiT and VAE resident. Both experts stay on the GPU on H200-class cards and above; 80 GB cards keep streaming (the two bf16 experts alone are 53 GiB). This holds even when the tier cannot size the checkpoint.

What changes on common GPUs (single GPU unless noted; per-GPU weights at serving precision):

| Model | Weights per GPU | Tier at 2x | H100 80 GB (~79 GiB free) | H200 (~139 GiB free) | 32 GB RTX 5090 (~31 GiB free) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Z-Image-Turbo | 19.1 GiB | 38 GiB | all resident (text encoder was layerwise) | all resident | unchanged |
| FLUX.1-dev | 31.4 GiB | 63 GiB | all resident (T5 was layerwise) | all resident | unchanged |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 | 30.2 GiB | 60 GiB | all resident | all resident | unchanged |
| Qwen-Image | 53.7 GiB (TP2: 34.7) | 107 GiB (TP2: 69) | unchanged (TP2: all resident) | all resident | unchanged |
| Cosmos3-Nano | 32.5 GiB | 65 GiB | all resident | all resident | unchanged |
| Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B | 24.3 GiB (fp32 T5) | 49 GiB | all resident | all resident | unchanged |
| LTX-2 | 65.7 GiB | 131 GiB | unchanged | all resident | unchanged |
| Wan2.2-T2V-A14B | 74.9 GiB (fp32 T5) | 150 GiB | unchanged | both experts and VAE resident (threshold), T5 layerwise | unchanged |
| Ideogram-4 FP8, ModelOpt FP8/NVFP4 | not sized (quantized or `--transformer-path`) | | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged |

B200 (178 GiB free) and B300 (288 GiB) fit every bf16 row, Wan2.2-A14B included. Rows other than Z-Image-Turbo and Wan2.2-A14B follow from the sizing rule; they were not run.

Tests:
- `test_server_args.py`: Z-Image-Turbo keeps every component resident at 139 GiB free and at 45 GiB free (the bf16 serving size fits twice there, the fp32-stored bytes would not). 31 and 23 GiB free resolve exactly as an unsized checkpoint does. Batching, shared host/device memory and an unsized checkpoint keep the text encoder layerwise. Off CUDA, the tier replaces the whole-component text-encoder offload. Wan2.2-A14B keeps both experts and the VAE resident at 139 GiB free while T5 streams, and keeps everything resident at 280 GiB free with sizes.
- `test_weight_utils.py::TestCheckpointComponentSizes`: per-component sizes from a local layout and from a cached hub snapshot without network access; a partially downloaded snapshot (only `model_index.json`, as before the worker downloads), a missing shard, `.bin` weights or FP8 weights stay unsized.
- `conftest.mock_cuda_platform` and the server-args helper stub the sizing, so tests that construct `ServerArgs` for a real repo id never read the runner's HF cache.
- Docs: the `auto` row of the performance-mode table in the deployment cookbook describes the tier.

The new tests fail on main: the sizing helper does not exist there, and the all-resident, serving-precision, off-CUDA and Wan2.2 assertions fail on their own.

## Accuracy Tests

Placement only: the same modules run on the same device, so outputs do not change. On 1xH200, Z-Image-Turbo outputs for five distinct prompts have the same md5s on main and this PR.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Z-Image-Turbo on 1xH200, flagless `sglang serve` (auto mode), 1024x1024, 9 steps. Each run: fresh server, 2 warmup requests, then 5 measured requests, each with a distinct prompt so the conditioning cache never answers the text encoder's work. Rounds interleaved main / PR / main / PR:

| | e2e median (round 1 / round 2) | `TextEncodingStage` | Peak memory per request |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (text encoder layerwise) | 0.952 / 0.954 s | 0.130 s | 15,456 MB |
| this PR (all resident) | 0.867 / 0.863 s | 0.031 s | 22,170 MB |

That is −9% end to end. Every PR sample is below every main sample (0.860–0.872 vs 0.950–1.008 s). The server logs `Auto memory policy for ZImagePipelineConfig: 139.3 GiB free on the least-free selected GPU holds the 19.1 GiB of weights per GPU at least 2x, so every component without an explicit placement stays resident.`

The same PR with all but 30 GiB of the GPU held by another process (the inputs of a 32 GB card) keeps main's placement: text encoder and VAE layerwise, DiT component-offloaded, `TextEncodingStage` 0.130 s.

Earlier evidence for the same gap: H100 Z-Image-Turbo, all resident 0.701/0.699 s vs auto 0.793/0.799 s (−12%).

Wan2.2-T2V-A14B, flagless on 1xH200 (startup only; no timed request): main streams both experts (`transformer` and `transformer_2`: 1.74 GB on the GPU, 26.18 GB pinned on the host each) and the text encoder. This PR loads both experts on the GPU (26.62 GB each) and keeps the VAE resident and the fp32 T5 layerwise, so 52 GB less pinned host memory per rank; the tier itself does not apply (150 GiB needed, 139 free). The end-to-end gain was not measured here.

## CI and baselines

The tier changes placement on the 80 GB H100 lanes wherever the checkpoint is cached and fits twice, so these scenarios will report higher `load_peak_vram_mb` / `runtime_peak_vram_mb` and fail the up-only 1%/2% memory checks by design. Their latency baselines may become stale-high (not a failure). Re-seed them with the usual two-step flow (first run prints the blocks to add to `perf_baselines/h100.json`):
- 1 GPU: `flux_image_t2i`, `zimage_image_t2i`, `zimage_image_t2i_multi_lora`, `cosmos3_nano_t2i`, `cosmos3_nano_t2v` (transformer already pinned resident; the small components join it), `sana_video_2b_t2v`, `longlive2_t2v`, `longlive2_i2v`, `fast_hunyuan_video` (38.5 GiB, 77 of ~79 GiB: closest to the line), `wan2_2_ti2v_5b`, `fastwan2_2_ti2v_5b`, `turbo_wan2_1_t2v_1.3b`, and the Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B family (`wan2_1_t2v_1.3b`, `_teacache_enabled`, `_frame_interp_2x`, `_upscaling_4x`, `_frame_interp_2x_upscaling_4x`, `wan2_1_t2v_1_3b_lora_1gpu`).
- 2 GPUs: `flux_image_t2i_2_gpus`, `zimage_image_t2i_2_gpus`, `zimage_image_t2i_2_gpus_non_square`, `qwen_image21_t2i_tp2`, `wan2_1_t2v_1.3b_cfg_parallel`, `wan2_1_t2v_1_3b_cache_dit_sp_only_2gpu`, `fsdp-inference`.
- `wan2_1_t2v_1.3b_encoder_permanent_residents` exists to test a permanent layerwise resident set on the text encoder, so it now pins the encoder layerwise with `--component-residency text_encoder=layerwise-offload`.
- Unchanged: the 5090 lane (nothing fits twice in ~31 GiB), every quantized or `--transformer-path` case, cases with explicit placement of the components that would move, Wan2.2-A14B, Qwen-Image 1-GPU, LTX and MiniMax-H3 on H100. The B200 lane runs only ModelOpt cases with `--transformer-path`/quantized weights.

The list comes from sizing each case's checkpoint at its serving precision against ~79 GiB free; a runner whose HF cache misses a model keeps main's placement for it.

## Risks

- Steady VRAM grows by the components that used to stream (Z-Image-Turbo +6.7 GB peak, the LTX-2 text encoder on H200, ~53 GiB of Wan2.2-A14B experts on H200). The factor of two leaves at least the weights' size free for activations, assuming one request at a time.
- A checkpoint that is not cached at startup is not sized, so a first start can place components differently from later ones. That is the same placement as main, never more resident.
- `ServerArgs` now reads safetensors headers of a cached checkpoint at startup (local files only, no network).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Turn on breakable CUDA graphs by default for LTX-2/LTX-2.3 two-stage serving
issues.body:
## Motivation

LTX-2 two-stage stage 1 runs at half resolution (~1.5k video tokens), so its step is launch-bound: on 4xB300, TRT-LLM's CUDA-graph configuration runs a stage-1 step in 0.044 s against 0.192 s for sglang eager. Breakable CUDA graphs (BCG) close most of that gap, and the graphs replay the same kernels, so the output is bitwise equal to eager. Today BCG is opt-in, so every flagless LTX deployment leaves this on the table.

BCG stays opt-in everywhere else. The validated-model list records correctness, not speed: FLUX.3 won 1 of 10 cells, Qwen-Image-2.1 on 1 GPU is 0.5% slower, and MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA showed no speedup.

| HW (2 GPUs, CFG parallel) | Model | Eager (s) | BCG (s) | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B300 | LTX-2 T2V 768x512x121, 40 steps | 6.693 / 6.882 | 3.797 / 3.785 | −44% |
| B300 | LTX-2.3 T2V 768x512x121, 30 steps | 6.294 / 6.202 | 4.735 / 4.726 | −24% |
| H200 | LTX-2 T2V 768x512x121, 40 steps | 7.398 / 7.593 | 5.969 / 5.970 | −20% |

B300 rows: two interleaved rounds, fresh server per arm. H200 rows: see Speed Tests.

## Modifications

- `ModelDeploymentConfig.bcg_default_pipeline_class_names`: the pipeline classes measured faster with BCG. `LTX2PipelineConfig` lists `LTX2TwoStagePipeline`; LTX-2.3 inherits it. The field names the pipeline class because one config serves the one-stage, two-stage and HQ pipelines, and only two-stage was measured.
- `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph` defaults to unset. `_adjust_breakable_cuda_graph_support` resolves an unset flag to on only when all of these hold, and to off otherwise:
  - the pipeline class is opted in and the checkpoint is on the validated BCG list;
  - `--performance-mode` is `auto` or `speed`;
  - the platform is CUDA (`current_platform.is_cuda()`, so ROCm, NPU and MPS stay off) with separate host and device memory (GB10 stays off);
  - the server warms up at startup (`sglang serve`); `sglang generate` and request warmup would pay a full extra generation;
  - monolithic role, ComfyUI mode off;
  - no torch.compile, Cache-DiT, dynamic batching or `--lora-path`;
  - both stage DiTs stay resident: no DiT component, snapshot or layerwise offload, no FSDP, a GPU with at least 130 GiB (the threshold LTX already uses to pick `resident` mode), and LTX-2.3 in `resident` mode.
  An explicit `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph true|false` always wins. When the default turns BCG on, the server logs `[Diffusion BCG] enabled by default for LTX2TwoStagePipeline; pass --enable-breakable-cuda-graph false to run eager.`
- Video BCG warmup now captures the model's full default resolution. It used the server-warmup resolution, which caps video at 832x480: LTX's 768x512 fits under the cap, but Wan (1280x720), MiniMax-H3 (1344x768) or LTX-2.5 (1920x1088) would capture a shape no request uses. Frame counts already used the full default under BCG.
- Graphs replay the weights and LoRA branches they were captured with, and serving never re-captures. So an external LoRA change (`/v1/set_lora`, merge, unmerge) or `resume_memory_occupation` now drops the captured graphs, and later requests run eager with a warning. The two-stage pipeline's own per-request distilled-LoRA switch is part of the capture and is unaffected.
- Docs: CLI reference and the LTX cookbook describe the default, its gates and the captured shape.

Behavior to know about (one-shot `MISSED` warning, then eager; no regression against today's eager path):
- Only the captured shape replays: 768x512, 121 frames, the warmup's quality level, text-to-video. The OpenAI video API defaults to 4 seconds, which LTX rounds to 89 frames, so those requests run eager unless the server passes `--warmup-num-frames 89`. Image-conditioned requests run eager.
- A request at another quality level (for example `quality="exact"`) runs eager; the runners are already keyed per level.
- Per-request attention-backend overrides are rejected under BCG, as before.

Tests:
- `test_server_args.py::TestBreakableCudaGraphDefault`: flagless LTX-2 two-stage serving on a mocked 141 GiB CUDA GPU resolves BCG on and captures 768x512; LTX-2.3 needs `resident`; explicit off, offline runs, request warmup, memory/manual modes, compile, batching, `--lora-path`, ComfyUI, one-stage and HQ pipelines, unvalidated checkpoints, every DiT offload form, low free memory and an 80 GB card resolve it off; ROCm (`is_cuda()` false) and shared-memory devices stay off; explicit on elsewhere is unchanged.
- `test_cfg_parallel_warmup.py::test_bcg_capture_keeps_the_full_default_video_resolution`.
- `test_diffusion_bcg_padding.py::TestBCGWeightChangeAfterCapture`: `set_lora`, merge, unmerge and `resume_memory_occupation` drop the graphs, and the runner then runs eager.

On main the default-on, platform-gate, capture-shape and graph-drop tests fail; the gate-off cases pass there by construction and guard the gates from here on.

## Accuracy Tests

LTX-2 two-stage on 2xH200, CFG parallel, the benchmark-default command (`--performance-mode speed`), seed 42, 768x512x121. Same MP4 bytes and same decoded-frame md5 for every arm:

| Server | Request | Path | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| this PR, no BCG flag | default quality | BCG replay | `742a1862…` |
| this PR, `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph false` | default quality | eager | `742a1862…` |
| main | default quality | eager | `742a1862…` |
| this PR, no BCG flag | `quality="exact"` | eager (no graph at that level) | same as eager server |
| this PR, no BCG flag | API default, 89 frames | eager (`MISSED`) | same as eager server |
| this PR, no BCG flag | after `/v1/set_lora` | eager (graphs dropped) | same as eager server after the same call |

With the CI-shaped request (1 second = 25 frames, `quality="exact"`, `--warmup-num-frames 25 --warmup-sampling-params '{"quality": "exact"}'`), BCG, eager and main also produce identical outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

LTX-2 two-stage, 2xH200, CFG parallel, the benchmark-default command (`--performance-mode speed --dit-layerwise-offload false --enable-torch-compile false`, no BCG flag), 768x512x121, 40 steps. [diffusion-bench-framework](https://github.com/mickqian/diffusion-bench-framework) `single_e2e` (median of 2 measured requests after warmup), fresh server per run, rounds interleaved main / PR / main / PR:

| | round 1 | round 2 |
|---|---|---|
| main (eager) | 7.398 s | 7.593 s |
| this PR (BCG by default) | 5.969 s | 5.970 s |

Stage breakdown (round 2): `LTX2AVDenoisingStage` 5.368 → 3.702 s, `LTX2RefinementStage` 1.187 → 1.096 s, decode unchanged (0.67 s). On Hopper the FA attention calls stay eager, so each forward captures 289 segments; on B300 LTX attention is captured as well (1 segment per forward), which is why the gain there is about twice as large.

Cost on 2xH200, this PR with and without `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph false`, two alternating rounds:

| | BCG default | `--enable-breakable-cuda-graph false` |
|---|---|---|
| Startup to healthy (round 1 / round 2) | 104.1 / 84.1 s | 86.1 / 78.0 s |
| Server warmup | 121 frames, 40 steps: 52.1 / 32.2 s | 25 frames, 2 steps: 31.6 / 26.5 s |
| Peak memory per request (rank 0) | 82,654 MB | 75,690–75,704 MB |

Startup grows by about 6 s once caches are warm (about 20 s on a cold first start), and peak memory by 6.9 GB. On B300 the same comparison was +2 s and +0.95 GB (LTX-2) / +1.1 GB (LTX-2.3).

## CI and baselines

No perf or memory baseline should move:
- The H100 suite's LTX cases run on 80 GB cards, below the 130 GiB gate, so they stay eager. The B200, 5090 and XPU suites have no LTX two-stage case, and AMD is not CUDA.
- The explicit-BCG CI tests (`test_diffusion_bcg_*zimage_turbo.py`) are image models; the warmup-resolution change only affects video.
- If an H200/B200-class LTX two-stage case is added later, its runtime peak will include the capture (+~7 GB on Hopper), and its warmup runs one full generation; seed its baseline with the usual two-step flow.

## Risks

- Startup grows by one full-shape generation plus capture: +6 s on 2xH200 with warm caches, about +20 s on a cold first start, +2 s on B300.
- Peak memory grows by ~7 GB on Hopper, where attention stays eager (289 segments per signature), against ~1 GB on Blackwell, where LTX attention is captured too (1 segment). The 130 GiB gate keeps 80 GB cards, whose speed-mode headroom is smaller than that, on eager.
- LTX-2.3 is validated on B300 only (above). The H200 runs here cover LTX-2.
- #45943 changes the dynamic-LoRA linear path that stage 2 runs; BCG captures whatever eager runs, so outputs stay equal to eager, but its speed should be re-checked once both land.

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Serve FA4 head sizes on Blackwell instead of falling back to sm80 SDPA
issues.body:
## Motivation

The CUDA platform decides whether FlashAttention can serve a layer with `FlashAttentionBackend.get_supported_head_sizes()`. That is FA3's list: 32, 64, 96, ..., 256. On Blackwell the FA backend is FA4, which also serves every multiple of 8 up to 128. Other head sizes fall back to `torch_sdpa`. The CUDA platform disables cuDNN SDPA for the whole process, so PyTorch then runs its sm80 FlashAttention-2 kernel (`pytorch_flash::flash_fwd_kernel`).

The Qwen-VL vision towers hit this:
- Qwen3-VL has head size 72. It is the encoder of Qwen-Image-2.1 edit and MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA.
- Qwen2.5-VL has head size 80. It is the encoder of Qwen-Image and Qwen-Image-Edit.

It happens both with the default backend and with `--attention-backend fa`. In both cases the server log shows `Attention backends for text_encoder: torch_sdpa, ...`.

Kernel time on one B300, `[1, H, S, 72]` bf16, non-causal:

| H, S | sm80 FA2 (current) | cuDNN SDPA | FA4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16, 23808 | 9.64 ms | 2.37 ms | 2.35 ms |
| 8, 23808 | 5.09 ms | 1.27 ms | 1.27 ms |
| 16, 4096 | 0.340 ms | 0.082 ms | 0.106 ms |

## Modifications

`CudaPlatformBase._resolve_flash_attention_backend_cls_str`: on Blackwell, a head size that is a multiple of 8 up to 128 now counts as FA-capable, which matches FA4's own check for sm100.
- Default backend: these layers take the Blackwell default, `dynamic_cudnn_sdpa`. That is cuDNN SDPA, with FA4 as the fallback.
- `--attention-backend fa`: they run FA4, including its packed-varlen path.
- Hopper, SM12x and ROCm are unchanged.

Tests: `test_cuda_attention_backend.py` adds two cases on a mocked platform.
- Blackwell: head sizes 72 and 80 resolve to `dynamic_cudnn_sdpa` by default and to FA4 when FA is requested. Head sizes 68 and 136 still fall back to `torch_sdpa`. On main, the 72 and 80 subtests fail.
- Pre-Blackwell: head size 72 keeps `torch_sdpa`.

## Accuracy Tests

All three kernels take bf16 inputs and accumulate in fp32. Against an fp32 reference on random inputs (H=16, S=23808, D=72), their max abs error is 2.8e-4 (sm80 FA2), 2.7e-4 (cuDNN) and 2.5e-4 (FA4).

The table compares the vision tower's outputs on main and on this PR, with the real checkpoints and the same request inputs. Each value is the relative L2 difference.

| | deepstack (block 8) | deepstack (block 16) | deepstack (block 24) | merger output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA, 2976x2048 reference, cuDNN | 1.3% | 2.4–2.5% | 3.7–3.8% | 4.7–4.8% |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 edit, `--attention-backend fa` (FA4) | 1.2% | 2.2–2.3% | 3.3–3.6% | 7.1–8.3% |
| Qwen-Image-2.1 edit, default backend (cuDNN) | 1.2% | 2.2–2.3% | 3.4–3.6% | 6.7–7.7% |

The difference grows steadily with depth, which is how bf16 rounding differences add up over 27 blocks. No single layer jumps.

Each kernel against an fp32 reference. The Qwen3-VL vision tower of Qwen-Image-2.1 (27 blocks, head size 72) ran on the benchmark's edit reference (1248x864 after the stage's resize, 4212 patches), once with fp32 weights and math SDPA as the reference, and once in bf16 per attention kernel. Only the attention kernel changes between the bf16 rows. Each value is the relative L2 difference from the fp32 reference, on one B300:

| bf16 attention kernel | deepstack (block 8) | deepstack (block 16) | deepstack (block 24) | merger output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sm80 FlashAttention-2 (main on Blackwell) | 2.40% | 5.34% | 7.68% | 15.09% |
| cuDNN SDPA (this PR, default backend) | 2.40% | 5.50% | 7.84% | 13.86% |
| FA4 (this PR, `--attention-backend fa`) | 2.40% | 5.21% | 7.55% | 14.91% |
| memory-efficient SDPA (for scale) | 2.39% | 5.27% | 7.64% | 15.24% |

The new kernels are as close to fp32 as main's kernel. FA4 is closer at every depth. cuDNN is within 0.2 points at the deepstack taps and closer at the output. The 7-8% kernel-to-kernel difference in the earlier table is the size of bf16 rounding over 27 blocks, the same order as each kernel's distance from fp32. (The same check on H200 gives FlashAttention-2 / cuDNN / memory-efficient at 14.39% / 15.28% / 15.20% for the merger output.)

End to end on B300 (Qwen-Image-2.1 edit, B300 `--attention-backend fa` command), this PR ran stacked with four other changes; that stack measured 2.626 / 2.637 s against main's 2.751 / 2.771 s. The changes measured on their own account for all but ~60-67 ms of that difference, which is the stored-PNG change plus this one.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Server runs on B300 with each case's serving command. Main and this PR ran side by side on separate GPUs, with requests sent one at a time. The vision-tower time is synchronized wall time around the tower's forward, and the kernel times come from `torch.profiler`.

**MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA**, 2 GPUs with Ulysses 2. The encoder is TP-folded to 8 heads per rank. The reference is 2976x2048, which gives 23808 patches over 27 blocks.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| attention kernels per tower forward | 137.5 ms (27x `pytorch_flash::flash_fwd_kernel`, sm80) | 34.2 ms (27x `cudnn_generated_fort_native_sdpa_sm100_flash_fprop`) |
| vision tower | 182–188 ms | 84.5–84.7 ms |
| text-encoding stage, two warm requests | | 116 ms and 107 ms shorter |
| end to end, 50 steps | 103.41 s | 102.99 s |

**Qwen-Image-2.1 edit**, 1 GPU. The reference becomes 4212 patches over 27 blocks.

| | main | this PR, `--attention-backend fa` | this PR, default backend |
|---|---|---|---|
| attention kernels per tower forward | 9.4 ms | 2.9 ms (FA4) | 2.3 ms (cuDNN) |
| vision tower | 21.0–21.5 ms | 18.0–20.8 ms | 14.5–16.7 ms |

For this case the vision tower is a small share of the encoding stage. Encoding-stage and end-to-end times stayed within run-to-run noise.

The first request at a new image size pays for building a cuDNN plan once per sequence length, about 45 ms. On the H3 case's first request the tower took 128 ms on this PR, against 182 ms on main. FA4 builds no per-shape plan.
