issues.title: [Perf] diffusion/qwen-image-2.1: Keep an image prefix's K/V in the packed buffer across steps
issues.body:
## Motivation

Qwen-Image-2.1 computes the prompt prefix (text, and for edits the reference image tokens) once per request and caches its per-layer K/V. Every cached denoising step still rebuilds the attention input from scratch: the packed projection allocates a fresh `[P+S, 3C]` QKV buffer per layer, and the fused Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE + pack kernel copies the cached prefix K/V into its first `P` rows before attention.

For text-to-image the prefix is a few dozen rows and the copy is free. For an edit the reference image makes the prefix about as long as the target (1248x864 reference: 4212 image rows plus text, against 4096 target rows), so the copy doubles the kernel's memory traffic in every layer of every step. On 1xH200 the kernel takes 164 us per call in an edit request against 95 us in a text-to-image request (grid capped at 65535 instead of 32984 blocks): about 88 ms per 40-step request across 32 layers.

## Modifications

`models/dits/qwen_image21.py`, `QwenImage21Attention`:
- After an image-conditioned prefill on the packed path, the request's per-layer cache keeps the packed buffer (`cache["qkv"]`), and its `key`/`value` become views of that buffer's prefix rows, so the separate prefix tensors are freed.
- Cached steps project into the kept buffer (the GEMM writes rows `[P:]` exactly as before) and call the same CUDA kernel with an empty prefix on the target rows, so it normalizes and rotates Q and the target K in place and copies nothing. Attention reads the full buffer.
- Text-only prefixes keep today's compact copy. The kept path needs the packed projection and a verified CUDA pack kernel, single sample, no SP, and no BCG prefix padding; anything else runs as before.

The attention inputs are the same values in the same layout, so outputs are bitwise unchanged. Memory: an edit request holds `[P+S, 3C]` bf16 per layer instead of the `[P, 2C]` prefix plus one transient buffer, about 3.1 GB more at the 1024x1024 edit shape.

Tests (`test_qwen_image21_cuda.py`, CUDA):
- `test_cached_steps_copy_the_prefix_only_for_text`: records every pack-kernel call over a prefill and two cached steps. For an image prefix the cached steps pass an empty prefix and write into the buffer kept by the prefill; for a text prefix they copy the prefix as before.
- `test_cuda_qk_rope_pack_matches_eager_prefill_and_cached_steps`: still bitwise against the eager chain on prefill and cached steps and under BCG replay; its storage check now expects an image prefix to live in the kept buffer and a text prefix to stay compact.

## Accuracy Tests

1xH200, the harness's Qwen-Image-2.1 edit and text-to-image requests: decoded output pixels are bitwise identical to main (md5 of 3 edit and 2 text-to-image outputs, stacked with the other changes listed below).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

1xH200, Qwen-Image-2.1 edit 1024, fresh servers, two GPUs alternated, client medians of 5 (base = main + stored PNG + parallel digest; this column also has the threaded condition resize, see the per-change split below):

| 1 | 5.262 s | 5.176 / 5.174 s |

|---|---|---|---|
| 1xH200, 8 rounds | 5.222 s | 5.155 s | −68 ms |
| 1xB300 (`--attention-backend fa`), 6 rounds | 2.657 s | 2.603 s | −50 ms |

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: Serve image responses from in-memory encoded bytes
issues.body:
## Motivation

`/v1/images/generations` and `/v1/images/edits` spend avoidable time after the image is decoded:

1. **A disk round trip per image.** The output rank encodes the image into a file under the output directory, and the HTTP server then reads that file back to base64 it. With `--output-path ""` nothing is persisted, so the file goes to a per-request temp dir purely as a transport.
2. **A slow PNG encode.** PNG is deflated at zlib level 1 on the output rank, single-threaded. For a 1024x1024 image that is tens of milliseconds on the request's critical path, while level 0 produces the same pixels several times faster.

## Modifications

- `entrypoints/utils.py`: an image is encoded once, in memory (`_encode_image_frame`). `save_materialized_output` writes those bytes when saving and, with `return_image_bytes`, returns them even when nothing is written. `save_outputs` / `post_process_sample` collect them through `image_bytes_out`.
- PNG defaults to zlib level 0: same pixels, about 3x the bytes of level 1 on typical generations, several times faster to encode. An `output_compression` other than 75 still selects a level. JPEG and WebP go through the same imageio call into memory instead of into a file, and their bytes are unchanged.
- New sampling field `return_image_bytes` (default off, set by `/v1/images`). The output rank also encodes when `save_output` is off but the bytes are requested, and returns them in `OutputBatch.output_image_bytes`. The scheduler slices them per request when it splits a dynamic batch, and the API-side save path fills the same field.
- `image_api.py`: b64_json responses are built from `output_image_bytes`; no file is read back. A file is written only when the server persists outputs (`--output-path`, default `outputs/`) or uploads them to cloud storage, and the persisted file holds exactly the returned bytes. `file_path`, `/v1/images/{id}/content` and url responses are unchanged. GLM-Image's actual output size is read from the bytes.
- Docs: the `--async-output-save` scope now includes `return_image_bytes` requests, and the output-quality notes describe the PNG level.

Tradeoff: PNG responses and persisted PNG files are larger (1024x1024: Z-Image-Turbo RGB 1.60 → 3.15 MB, Qwen-Image-2.1 RGBA 1.83 → 4.20 MB; the b64_json body grows by 4/3 of that). Pass `output_compression` to trade encode time for size.

Tests (`test_image_response_bytes.py`):
- the returned PNG decodes to the source pixels exactly for 2-D grayscale, single-channel, RGB and RGBA frames, at the default and at explicit levels, and no file is written when `save_output` is off;
- a saved file holds exactly the returned bytes (PNG, JPEG, WebP), and JPEG/WebP bytes equal what the previous file writer produced;
- the worker returns one encoded image per output and writes the file only when saving; it encodes when either saving or returning bytes;
- a split dynamic batch keeps each request's bytes;
- both image endpoints answer b64_json from the returned bytes without a file, and request a file only when the server persists outputs.

## Accuracy Tests

Same request (seed 42, `output_format=png`, b64_json) against both arms:

issues.body:
## Motivation

Two blocking device reads sit on the host's critical path:

1. **Cosmos3, every step.** The denoising loop checked the CFG window, and the Transfer control-CFG window, with `t.item()` on the device timestep. So the host waited for each step's kernels to finish before it launched the next step.
2. **Qwen-Image-2.1 edit, every request.** The edit path built the VAE latent mean/std with `new_tensor` right after launching the condition-image VAE encode. That pageable upload made the host wait for the encode before it could start the prompt's image preprocessing.

## Modifications

- `cosmos3.py`: the loop takes one host copy of the timestep schedule (`timesteps.tolist()`), and `_cfg_active_at` reads the window from those floats. The per-step decisions and kernels are unchanged.
- `qwen_image21.py`: `QwenImage21EncodingStage` uploads the latent mean/std once per `(dtype, device)` and reuses them, so the preprocessing overlaps the encode. The normalization is bit-identical.

Tests:
- `test_cosmos3_rollout.py::test_cfg_window_check_reads_host_timesteps`: runs the denoising loop with a `[400, 1000]` CFG window over timesteps whose `item()` / `float()` / `bool()` raise. The window must still choose batched CFG at 999, 700 and 400, and the cond branch alone at 399 and 100. It fails on main.
- `test_qwen_image21.py::test_condition_latents_reuse_uploaded_latent_stats`: two edit requests must produce the reference-normalized condition latents bitwise, and the second request must reuse the first one's mean/std tensors (checked by identity).

No files are shared with #45942, #45943, #45944 or #45948.

The output pixels are identical across arms for both models.

issues.title: [Fix] diffusion/lora: Preserve eager base dispatch for disabled and merged adapters
issues.body:
## Motivation

`BaseLayerWithLoRA` keeps its disabled/merged pass-through eager and compiles only the dynamic adapter path, because layerwise offload can rebind weights. `LinearWithLoRA` instead decorates its entire `forward` with `torch.compile`: wrapping an ordinary `nn.Linear` changes the base dispatch even when no adapter is active or after it is disabled. Compilers may choose a different GEMM/bias fusion; this also defeats the shared class's offload precaution.

The AMD Qwen Image 2.1 LoRA tests in [this run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37030627223/job/110916375120) fail exact base-output restoration by 1.1920928955078125e-7. This PR addresses the concrete dispatch inconsistency; whether it resolves that AMD numerical failure still needs native CI confirmation.

## Modifications

- Mirror `BaseLayerWithLoRA`: directly invoke the original base layer when disabled or merged, and apply merged output offsets eagerly when present.
- Keep compilation on the active dynamic LoRA path.
- Add disabled/merged × absent/present offset coverage, exact output checks and repeated weight rebinds. A compiler-sensitive value witness verifies that the pass-through really uses eager dispatch (a Python assertion alone can graph-break and miss this regression).

## Accuracy Tests

Synced with current main `913e91ed`, candidate `1b43c169`; isolated RTX 5090 D v2, Python 3.12 / PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130:

- **114 passed**, no skips, across complete inference-mode, commit-as-base, dynamic-delta-in-GEMM and auto-merge-rounding files.
- All 958 imported repository files match the merged source. Changed-file pre-commit and diff checks pass.
- Retains upstream chunked `addmm_` merge and exact/unit-scale coverage alongside eager disabled/merged/zero-scale dispatch regressions.
- Historical failure witness on the original production code: 4 failed / 2 passed; the four pass-through cases fail. This predates the current main sync.

Native AMD output restoration is still unverified. No tolerance is relaxed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput improvement claimed. Dynamic LoRA remains compiled; merged/disabled linear layers now use the base dispatch, matching the existing parallel-linear wrapper policy. A full-model AMD latency/accuracy comparison requires upstream hardware CI.

## Checklist

- [x] Changed-file pre-commit checks pass.
- [x] Regression tests added and related CUDA tests pass.
- [x] Accuracy results and platform limits documented.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style.
- [ ] Native AMD CI (requires maintainer authorization).

issues.body: ## Motivation Add native support for [Wan-Animate-2 Distilled](https://huggingface.co/Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Distilled-Diffusers) (`Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Distilled-Diffusers`), the distilled variant of the 14B character-animation model of the Wan2.2 family. Like the base checkpoint it takes a **reference image** and a **reference video** and produces a clip of the reference subject performing the reference video's motion; the distilled checkpoint does it in 10 steps at `guidance_scale` 1.0 instead of 40 steps with CFG 3.0. Builds on #42941. The distilled checkpoint is served by the same native `WanAnimate2Pipeline`, selected automatically from the checkpoint directory, as configuration on top of the base support: `log_scale = -1.3` in the attention score modifier, 10 steps at `guidance_scale` 1.0, no CFG parallelism, DPM-Solver++ as the [official](https://github.com/Wan-Video/Wan-Animate-2) command-line implementation samples it. ## Modifications ### New - `Wan_Animate_2_14B_Distilled_Config` (`configs/pipeline_configs/wan.py`): the DiT config with `log_scale` -1.3, the official distillation yaml value (a `log_scale` key in the checkpoint's `transformer/config.json` still wins), and `supports_cfg_parallel=False`. `Wan_Animate_2_14B_Distilled_SamplingParam` (`configs/sample/wan.py`): 10 steps, `guidance_scale` 1.0, everything else inherited from the base sampling params. - `WanAnimate2SchedulerLoader`: the distilled checkpoint is sampled with DPM-Solver++ 2M on the Wan sigma grid, like the base checkpoint, because that is what the model authors' command-line implementation runs for both checkpoints (their distilled yaml's `flow_solver: euler` key is read by no code). The `FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler` named in the distilled repo's `scheduler/scheduler_config.json` is read only by the Diffusers pipeline, which also omits the distilled `log_scale` bias. The loader builds DPM-Solver++ for the distilled config without reading that file and loads the checkpoint's `scheduler/` for the base config; it sets `component_names = []` so it stays pipeline-local, like `WanAnimate2TransformerLoader`; the existing loader-registry test covers both. On the same seed DPM-Solver++ lands 1.8 dB closer to the authors' command-line output than Euler on the shipped grid (33.2 against 31.4 dB, at the same cost): the choice matches the authors' executable implementation; it is not a quality ranking. `--scheduler-class-override` is ignored for the distilled checkpoint and one warning says so (the base checkpoint still honours it). - Registry detectors: both repos share the `model_index.json` `_class_name`; the variant is named only by the `_class_name` of `modular_model_index.json`. The distilled detector matches `WanAnimate2DistilledModularPipeline` or a Wan-Animate-2 path whose directory name carries a `distill` token (a token in a parent directory does not count), the base detector the rest, the distilled one registered first because a directory with `model_index.json` matches both through the shared class. `--model-id Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Distilled-Diffusers` pins the variant explicitly. - Cookbook page `docs/cookbook/diffusion/Wan/Wan-Animate-2.mdx`: variant table, defaults note, distilled presets, request examples, the GB200 distilled benchmark section and troubleshooting entries. The command picker config `docs/src/snippets/configs/Wan/wan-animate-2.jsx` gains a **Checkpoint weights** option in the shape of the Qwen-Image 2.1 Turbo one (#43391): per-checkpoint defaults and Request command, CFG parallelism disabled, **Auto** topology resolving to Ulysses and **Auto** text encoder to CPU offload for the distilled checkpoint, the nine measured GB200 layouts as verified recipes, covered by `docs/scripts/tests/wan-animate-2-config.test.mjs`. The model catalog lists both ids. - Unit tests in `test/unit/test_wan_animate_2_config.py` (the two configs, the loader, the CFG-parallel rejection, the `guidance_scale` rejection) and routing in `test_registry.py`; the unit tests run offline on CPU. One GPU CI case, `wan2_2_animate_2_14b_distilled_ref2v` (1 GPU, H100): the base case's inputs at the distilled recipe, at the default video consistency thresholds, with a perf scenario. ### Shared code touched - `registry.py`: the modular-index probe, a pure addition. For a local directory that ships `modular_model_index.json`, the detectors are also probed with that file's `_class_name`; unit test in `test_registry.py`. Nothing else outside the Wan-Animate-2 files changes. ### Supported features - Everything the base pipeline supports in #42941 except CFG parallelism: server warmup, Ulysses, TP and TP x Ulysses, text-encoder CPU offload, DiT layerwise offload (never changes a layout's output, about 2 s in the table below), per-request audio, the bf16 DiT with fp32 encoders and VAE. - Server warmup (`--warmup-mode server`, the `sglang serve` default): three synthetic one-clip startup requests with a built-in reference image and a generated silent reference video: the bounded warmup shape, a residency probe at the largest supported budget, 720x1280, that decides whether the DiT stays resident, and the bounded shape again. A request whose frame geometry differs from the warmup shapes pays a one-time flex-attention autotune on its first occurrence (about 16 s on 1 GPU, 12 to 13 s on 2, 9 s on 4); with `--warmup-mode off` or `request` the first real request pays it instead. - Multi-GPU: at `guidance_scale` 1.0 the CFG-parallel auto-enable rule does not fire, so `--num-gpus N` resolves to Ulysses (`--ulysses-degree N`); `--tp-size N` and `--tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2` work as on the base checkpoint. ### Notes on model-specific parameters - The base model's parameters are unchanged (`clip_len`, `fps`, `prompt_ref`, `size` as a pixel-area budget, `video_path` / `video_url`, `seconds` and `num_frames` ignored); the distilled checkpoint changes only the defaults: `num_inference_steps` 10 and `guidance_scale` 1.0. - `guidance_scale` other than 1.0 is rejected at request admission (see **Rejected at startup or request admission**): the distilled checkpoint samples at 1.0 only. - `log_scale` is not a request parameter: it comes from the config class (-1.3) or from the checkpoint's `transformer/config.json` when that file carries the key. ### Rejected at startup or request admission - CFG parallelism for the distilled config, with `Wan_Animate_2_14B_Distilled_Config does not support CFG parallelism`: there is one branch per step, nothing to split. - `guidance_scale` other than 1.0 for the distilled checkpoint, at request admission by the per-request validation hook (`ValueError`, HTTP 400 on `/v1/videos`): `guidance_scale= is not supported by the distilled Wan-Animate-2 checkpoint: it samples at guidance_scale 1.0 only (the distilled recipe has no unconditional branch); omit the field or set it to 1.0.` - Everything the base pipeline rejects in #42941 (`--ring-degree` above 1, `--use-fsdp-inference`, degrees that do not divide the 40 heads, an explicit `--attention-backend`, MXFP8 attention, `enable_teacache` / `enable_spectrum`, `use_img_emb=false`, any `--disagg-role`). ### Deviations from the native-support contract The per-request contract is kept as-is from the base model implementation. The one deviation this PR adds: the distilled checkpoint's scheduler is built in code by `WanAnimate2SchedulerLoader` instead of being read from the checkpoint's `scheduler/`, because the shipped config names a sampler the official reference implementation does not use (see the DPM-Solver++ rationale above). ## Accuracy Tests Inputs of the comparison below, the base PR's inputs, identical for both implementations. | Input 1: reference image (the subject to animate) | Input 2: reference video, 7.9 s at 30 fps (the motion to follow) | | --- | --- | || https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48c9939c-dd47-4800-a3ee-ed635a03eb3f | **Output, side by side:** sglang distilled (this PR) on the left, the official implementation with the distilled yaml on the right, seed 123. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc06693e-466e-4b3b-ae69-6e7bfc9ad718 **Output, frame grid at matching timestamps:** sglang distilled top row, official distilled middle row, official distilled with `log_scale` 0 bottom row. Same inputs in both implementations: a 16:9 reference image and a 7.9 s reference video at 30 fps, `size` 640x800 (a 960x528 frame), `clip_len` 37, 10 steps, `guidance_scale` 1.0, identical prompt and negative prompt, default reference-branch prompt; official = the official implementation with the distilled yaml, 236 aligned frames. sglang vs official is 32.8 dB mean PSNR at seed 123 and 31.9 dB at seed 124, while two seeds of either implementation are about 21 dB apart: the two implementations sample the same point, 11 to 12 dB above the two-seed floor, and the floors coincide. | Pair | PSNR mean / min (dB) | SSIM | LPIPS | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | | sglang vs official, seed 123 | 32.8 / 20.7 | 0.945 | 0.035 | | sglang vs official, seed 124 | 31.9 / 20.6 | 0.940 | 0.038 | | sglang seed 124 vs seed 123 (two-seed floor) | 21.0 / 19.1 | 0.780 | 0.126 | | official seed 124 vs seed 123 (two-seed floor) | 20.9 / 18.9 | 0.755 | 0.128 | | sampler A/B, seed 123: DPM-Solver++ on the official grid (this PR) vs official | 33.2 / 20.6 | 0.948 | - | | sampler A/B, seed 123: Euler on the shipped grid vs official | 31.4 / 20.8 | 0.941 | - | - The official code ran on the same GB200 node in bf16 with torch SDPA in place of flash-attn (the flex-attention path that applies `log_scale` was untouched). The band set before measuring for a same-sample match was 22 to 28 dB; the distilled pairs clear it. The same harness on the base checkpoint (40 steps, CFG 3.0) matched sglang's base output at 20.2 dB mean, the two-seed-floor level; that comparison is not part of this PR. - `log_scale` matters: the official output with `log_scale` 0 is 27.2 dB from its `-1.3` output, and sglang's `-1.3` output is closer to the official `-1.3` output (32.8 dB) than to the official `log_scale`-0 output (26.8 dB). - Sampler A/B at seed 123 (the last two table rows; they use a different frame resize, hence 33.2 against 32.8 dB for the same pair). Rows of the grid: DPM-Solver++ on the official grid (this PR), Euler on the shipped grid, official. - Within sglang: DiT layerwise offload and `sglang generate` are byte-identical to the resident 1-GPU server output, and the second request of every server reproduces the first (same md5). Multi-GPU layouts against 1 GPU with the default encoder and VAE parallel settings, PSNR mean / min dB: Ulysses 2 37.4 / 34.7, TP 2 35.9 / 32.4, Ulysses 4 33.3 / 26.4, TP 2 x Ulysses 2 34.8 / 29.7, TP 4 36.8 / 34.5; layerwise offload never changes a layout's output. - Context only: the distilled 10-step output against the base checkpoint's 40-step CFG-3.0 output on the same seed is 16.7 dB, the base model's two-seed-floor level, i.e. a different sample of the same scene. Base checkpoint at 40 steps (left) against the distilled checkpoint at 10 steps (right), and the grid base-40 / distilled-10 / base at 10 steps and guidance 1.0: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0bfe3c98-5e9f-4840-8517-aa1f2accc226 - CI case on H100: six same-tree generations were bit-identical (`Min SSIM: 1.0000 Min PSNR: inf Max mean_abs_diff: 0.0000`). The case uses the file's video defaults (CLIP 0.90, SSIM 0.92, PSNR 24 dB, mean abs diff 10.0), like the base case. The ground-truth frames are taken from the first CI run. How to run: ```bash # CPU unit tests (configs, loader, routing, CFG-parallel rejection, guidance rejection) pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_wan_animate_2_config.py \ python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_registry.py # GPU CI case (consistency against the H100 ground truth + perf check) pytest -s python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/server/test_server_1_gpu.py -k wan2_2_animate_2_14b_distilled_ref2v # Serve sglang serve --model-path Wan-AI/Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Distilled-Diffusers --text-encoder-cpu-offload ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Tested on 1, 2 and 4 GPUs of a 4x GB200 node (189 GB per GPU). Workload: the base PR's workload at the distilled defaults: 10 steps, `guidance_scale` 1.0, fps 30, 237 frames = 7 clips of 37, 640x800 budget on a 16:9 reference image (960x528 frame), seed 123, `sglang serve --text-encoder-cpu-offload --warmup-mode server`, two identical `/v1/videos` requests per server. E2E is the steady state (the second request); peak is the `nvidia-smi` maximum over ranks during the request, in the cookbook's unit (GiB column, `nvidia-smi` MiB / 1000, as the base table reports it). This is the cookbook's distilled GB200 benchmark. | Config | GPUs | Flags (plus `--text-encoder-cpu-offload`) | E2E (s) | Peak per GPU (GiB) | | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | | 1 GPU, DiT resident | 1 | none | 150.2 | 69.5 | | 1 GPU, layerwise DiT offload | 1 | `--dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer` | 150.0 | 39.7 | | 2 GPU, Ulysses2 (framework default) | 2 | `--ulysses-degree 2` | 87.0 | 60.1 | | 2 GPU, Ulysses2, layerwise DiT offload | 2 | `--ulysses-degree 2 --dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer` | 86.3 | 31.4 | | 2 GPU, TP2 | 2 | `--tp-size 2` | 97.1 | 40.0 | | 4 GPU, Ulysses4 (framework default) | 4 | `--ulysses-degree 4` | 55.8 | 51.0 | | 4 GPU, Ulysses4, layerwise DiT offload | 4 | `--ulysses-degree 4 --dit-layerwise-offload --layerwise-offload-components transformer` | 58.0 | 21.5 | | 4 GPU, TP2 x Ulysses2 | 4 | `--tp-size 2 --ulysses-degree 2` | 59.3 | 35.3 | | 4 GPU, TP4 | 4 | `--tp-size 4` | 64.1 | 30.4 | Speedups: - Ulysses is the fastest layout, 1.73x over 1 GPU on 2 GPUs (87.0 s vs 150.2 s) and 2.69x on 4 (55.8 s); the tensor-parallel layouts are slower (97.1, 59.3 and 64.1 s). - Layerwise DiT offload costs about 2 s and leaves the output identical while cutting the request-phase peak from 69.5 to 39.7 GiB on 1 GPU, 60.1 to 31.4 GiB on 2 and 51.0 to 21.5 GiB on 4. - The gain over the base checkpoint is structural (4x fewer steps, one branch per step). Every row's first request is 9 to 17 s slower than the steady state: the one-time flex-attention autotune fires because the request's frame geometry differs from the warmup shapes, plus other one-time costs. Whole-run peaks, which include the server warmup's synthetic requests (one at the largest supported budget, 720x1280, to decide whether the DiT stays resident), are higher: 95.5 / 64.8 / 72.3 / 41.9 / 47.3 / 57.4 / 27.3 / 38.9 / 37.8 GiB in row order. - `--enable-torch-compile` on 1 GPU brings no gain: 156.8 s steady state against 150.2 s eager, 1168 s for the first compiled request, 85.9 GiB peak, output 37.5 dB PSNR from eager and identical across requests. ### Recommended parallelism config It is recommended to use `--text-encoder-cpu-offload`. issues.title: [Feat] ComfyUI: Add online INT8 quantization for BF16 Qwen-Image-2.1 single files
issues.body:
## Motivation

Users on 24 to 32 GB GPUs often already have the BF16 ComfyUI file for Qwen-Image-2.1 but cannot use online quantization with it. Today they have to find and download a separate pre-quantized file.

Two things blocked this:

1. The plugin preflight rejected `quantization` for any ComfyUI single file.
2. The worker's single-file loader (`comfyui_checkpoints/spec.py`) only built a quant config from per-layer markers in the file. A BF16 file has none, so `--quantization` was silently ignored and the DiT stayed in BF16.

## Modifications

- `runtime/loader/comfyui_checkpoints/spec.py`: when a single file has no quant markers and `quantization` is set, resolve it through the existing `resolve_transformer_quant_load_spec` (same path native directories use), build the matching `WeightLoadPlan`, and run the quant post-load hooks. Methods that need serialized weights (e.g. `mxfp8`) raise a clear error instead of being ignored.
- Plugin `core/preflight.py`: allow `convrot_int8` on BF16 Qwen-Image-2.1 single files. Other models and other methods stay rejected with a clear message.
- Options tooltip and README updated.
- Tests: worker regression test (quant config, param dtype, load device and hooks reach the loader) and preflight accept/reject cases.

Scope is Qwen-Image-2.1 + INT8 ConvRot only. FP8 was tested and left out (results below). Other single-file models can be added once validated.

## Accuracy and speed (Modal, L40S)

ComfyUI v0.41.0, headless API graph through `SGLDUNETLoader` + `SGLDOptions`. `Comfy-Org/Qwen-Image-2.1` turbo file, 1024x1024, 8 steps, euler/simple, cfg 1, seed 42. Time is the second (warm) run. Peak GPU is whole-process `nvidia-smi` (includes ComfyUI's text encoder and VAE). PSNR/SSIM are against SGLD BF16 on the same seed.

| Run | Sampling time | Peak GPU | PSNR / SSIM vs SGLD BF16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Native ComfyUI BF16 | 3.43 s | 22.9 GB | 28.19 dB / 0.969 |
| SGLD BF16 | 3.29 s | 26.9 GB | reference |
| **SGLD online INT8 (this PR)** | **2.35 s** | 23.5 GB | **28.55 dB / 0.966** |
| SGLD online FP8 (not enabled) | 4.49 s | 23.5 GB | 21.74 dB / 0.855 |

Worker log for the INT8 run:

```
convrot_int8: quantized 224 linear layers (13.00 GiB of BF16 weights -> 6.50 GiB INT8; jit 0, comfy_kitchen 224), left 0 in BF16
```

INT8 is about 1.4x faster than BF16 and halves DiT weight memory, and its distance from BF16 is in line with native ComfyUI vs SGLD BF16. On L40S (CC 8.9) the JIT INT8 kernels are unavailable, so this ran on the comfy_kitchen backend.

### Why FP8 is not enabled

Online FP8 quantizes the same 224 layers but drifts from BF16 and is slower than BF16 on L40S. Keeping some layers in BF16 (`--quantization-ignored-layers`) did not fix it consistently (2 seeds each):

| FP8 variant | Time | SSIM (seed 42 / 1234) | PSNR dB (seed 42 / 1234) |
|---|---|---|---|
| BF16 reference | 3.17 s | | |
| FP8, all layers | 4.36 s | 0.855 / 0.854 | 21.7 / 20.8 |
| keep `img_mlp.out` in BF16 | 3.75 s | 0.814 / 0.866 | 20.6 / 21.7 |
| keep `attn.to_out` in BF16 | 4.18 s | 0.915 / 0.876 | 24.0 / 21.4 |
| keep both | 3.55 s | 0.879 / 0.884 | 22.6 / 21.8 |
| keep blocks 0 and 31 in BF16 | 4.23 s | 0.955 / 0.881 | 27.2 / 22.0 |

So the plugin rejects `fp8` for single files for now.

### Pre-quantized file note

Loading Comfy-Org's own `qwen_image_2.1_turbo_int8_convrot.safetensors` through `SGLDUNETLoader` fails on current main with `Parameter transformer_blocks.1.attn.comfy_attention.config not found in custom model state dict`. That is the serialized-marker path, which this PR does not touch; I can open a separate issue.

## Testing

- Unit tests on Modal (`test_comfyui_checkpoint_spec.py`, `test_comfyui_options.py`, `test_comfyui_generator.py`, `test_comfyui_qwen_image21.py`): 64 passed, 3 skipped.
- Same new tests against unmodified main: 5 failed (the 3 worker regression tests and 2 preflight cases), confirming they guard the change.
- End-to-end ComfyUI runs on L40S as above.

## Limitations

- Only Qwen-Image-2.1 single files are allowed in the plugin; Flux, Qwen-Image, Z-Image and MiniMax-H3 keep the existing rejection until validated.
- FSDP inference with online ConvRot INT8 on single files was not tested.

issues.title: [Fix] diffusion: Prevent int32 overflow in Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo VAE RMSNorm
issues.body:
## Motivation

The channel-first RMSNorm pointwise kernel in the Qwen-Image 2.1 VAE computes flattened offsets in int32. When `CHANNELS * SPATIAL` exceeds `INT32_MAX`, compilation can fail. A larger total element count across batches can also overflow the flattened index.

With SGLang's default `quality="lossless"` setting, Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo can fail when generating 4K images, reporting an error at `norm_index`:

`CompilationError: Scalar 2371092480 is out of range for type int32`.

Fixing the channel RMSNorm indexing allows generation to complete.

## Modifications

- Cast `program_id` to int64 **before** multiplying by `BLOCK` in `channel_rmsnorm_preserve_reduction.py`:
   ```python
   index = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
   ```

## Accuracy Tests

### Fix verification

`quality` uses the default `lossless` setting. The environment uses PyTorch 2.13.0 and Triton 3.7.1, with text-encoder CPU offload enabled and VAE tiling disabled. Both arms use the same model, inputs, seeds and eight-step configuration; only the indexing expression changes. All four cases below use an actual size of **3840×2144**. Before the fix, each fails to compile due to the int32 error and produces no image. After the fix, each completes one warmup and three measured requests; all four outputs within each case are byte-identical. Times are the means of the three measured requests. Raw request times and configurations are in `default-lossless-validation.json` in the bundle.

| Workload | Before | After | Fixed mean (s) |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Text-to-image | Failure | Success | 111.666 |
| One-reference edit | Failure | Success | 167.492 |
| Two-reference edit | Failure | Success | 235.382 |
| Three-reference edit | Failure | Success | 307.789 |


### Output equivalence

**Environment:** 1×H20 (SM90), Python 3.12.15, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, CUDA 13.0, Triton 3.8.0.

- **30 CUDA regression tests passed**, including full nonuniform BF16/FP16 tensors crossing `2**31`. All four full-tensor outputs match the Torch reference byte for byte.
- 4K text-to-image test with `quality` set to `exact`: **generation fails before the fix, with no image; after the fix, generation succeeds, and the warmup image and all three measured images exactly match the Torch norm reference images.**
- The 4K generation was confirmed to call the fixed channel RMSNorm function.

<details>
<summary>Regression coverage and reproduction</summary>

Full-tensor tests cover the large tensor used by a single 4K decode and tensors whose total element count across batches exceeds `2**31`, in BF16 and FP16. The reference is `F.normalize(x.float(), dim=1).to(dtype) * scale * weight + 0.0`. Whole-output byte checks cover channel and batch boundaries, offsets around the 32-bit index limit, and the tail.

Community-source model settings: BF16, 8 steps, seed 1042, CPU generator, guidance 1, `torch_sdpa`, TP1/SP1/CFG1; text-encoder CPU offload on. Workloads that generate successfully both before and after the fix use one warmup and three measured requests per arm. The reference images use the Torch implementation with this kernel’s optimized dispatch disabled; other settings are unchanged.

```bash
# In the SGLang checkout, with diffusion dependencies and at least 40 GiB free GPU memory:
SGLANG_REPO="$PWD"
pre-commit run --all-files
# Run standalone validation from the unpacked bundle using the tested source/environment:
cd /path/to/unpacked-validation-bundle
PYTHONPATH="$SGLANG_REPO/python" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
  SGLANG_TEST_LARGE_CHANNEL_RMSNORM=1 python -m pytest -v \
  files/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_channel_rmsnorm_preserve_reduction.py
PYTHONPATH="$SGLANG_REPO/python:$PWD/reproduce" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
  python reproduce/kernel_validation.py --repo "$SGLANG_REPO" --output "$PWD/kernel-replay"
PYTHONPATH="$SGLANG_REPO/python" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
  python reproduce/benchmark_graph.py "$SGLANG_REPO" "$PWD/graph-replay"
```

The validation bundle, [channel-rmsnorm-int64-pr-ready.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33653278/channel-rmsnorm-int64-pr-ready.zip), contains replay scripts, model configurations and raw records.

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Whole-model generation

Retested on one H20 using the community source and runtime above. For each quality setting, four fresh model instances run in this order: **before, after, after, before**. Each instance performs one warmup and three measured requests per workload. Each table value pools six measured requests from two instances.

SDK wall time includes preprocessing, IPC and PNG saving, excluding model loading and warmup. Values are **mean ± sample standard deviation**. Change = `(after / before − 1) × 100%`. **The table’s 24 measured before/after image pairs are identical in PNG bytes and RGBA pixels, with SSIM 1.**

| Quality | Workload | Size | Before (s) | After (s) | Mean time change |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| lossless | Text-to-image | 1024×1024 | 4.871 ± 0.350 | 4.757 ± 0.070 | -2.33% |
| lossless | One-reference edit | 1024×1024 | 6.305 ± 0.235 | 6.302 ± 0.296 | -0.05% |

| exact | One-reference edit | 1024×1024 | 6.252 ± 0.009 | 6.257 ± 0.026 | +0.08% |

<details>
<summary>Pointwise-kernel microbenchmark</summary>

Each CUDA graph captures 100 kernel launches; each timed event covers 10 replays. After warmup, before/after order alternates for 30 paired rounds. Values below are median GPU time per launch, not whole-model time. Shape order is batch, channels, time, height, width; four-dimensional inputs omit time.

</details>

These measurements cover the listed inputs on H20. Raw request times, image checks and graph samples are in `performance-recheck.json`.

issues.title: [diffusion] Share Qwen-Image 2.1 prefix KV across outputs of one prompt
issues.body:
## Motivation

Qwen-Image 2.1 prefills the condition prefix (text + reference-image latents) once per request and reuses its per-layer KV for every denoising step. With `num_outputs_per_prompt = n`, the encoding stage gives each output its own cache even though all `n` outputs of a prompt share the same encoder hidden states, layout and condition latents. The prefix is therefore prefilled `n` times and its KV is stored `n` times. The prefix is read-only after prefill, so the copies are redundant.

## Modifications

- `QwenImage21EncodingStage` builds one cache per prompt and hands the same object to every output of that prompt. Different prompts and the two guidance branches keep separate caches.
- `QwenImage21Transformer2DModel.forward` lets the first sample holding an empty cache prefill it; later samples holding the same cache skip the text projection and per-block prefix work and read the populated KV.
- Cookbook sentence on multi-output caches updated.

Scope: this only applies where one request keeps `n` outputs together, i.e. the HTTP image endpoints. Offline `sglang generate` expands `n` outputs into `n` single-output requests before the pipeline, so it is unaffected (measured: identical memory and latency). Requests crossing the disaggregation boundary rebuild independent caches, because the extras codec does not preserve object identity; that keeps today's behavior.

## Accuracy Tests

- New tests fail on main's implementation (3 failed) and pass here (3 passed); `test_qwen_image21.py` + `test_qwen_image21_cuda.py` pass in full (41 passed). The CUDA test asserts bitwise-equal output and KV versus independent caches and one prefill instead of two. pre-commit passes.
- Full checkpoint, `/v1/images/edits`, 1024x1024, 40 steps, seed 42, n in {1,2,4}, CFG off and CFG 4: all 14 output images are pixel-identical to main (max abs diff 0) on RTX PRO 6000; the same holds for the 10 images of the 5 configs main can run on RTX 5090, and for the same 10 on RTX 4090.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Protocol for every row: `/v1/images/edits`, one 1024x1024 reference image, 1024x1024 output, 40 steps, seed 42, fresh `sglang serve` per config, one warm request, peaks from `perf_dump_path` (`runtime_peak`, which is cumulative over the server's life and so includes the warm request of the same config). CFG rows use guidance 4 with a negative prompt. Latency is quoted per card; the cards are not comparable with each other.

Which stage owns the request peak depends on where the DiT lives during decode, so the effect differs by deployment.

**RTX 5090 32 GB, default flags** (auto policy: encoders and VAE layerwise-offloaded, `dit_cpu_offload`, so the DiT is off the GPU during decode and denoising is the peak). Two timed requests.

| config | peak allocated main -> here (MB) | latency main -> here (s) |
|---|---|---|
| CFG off, n=1 | 17653 -> 17653 | 16.86 / 16.94 -> 16.72 / 16.79 |
| CFG off, n=2 | 20256 -> 18068 | 32.78 / 32.59 -> 32.09 / 32.22 |
| CFG off, n=4 | 25469 -> 18967 | 65.27 / 65.37 -> 64.24 / 64.35 |
| CFG 4, n=1 | 19713 -> 19713 | 32.73 / 32.83 -> 32.75 / 32.84 |
| CFG 4, n=2 | 24374 -> 20129 | 63.85 / 63.99 -> 63.18 / 63.28 |
| CFG 4, n=4 | **OOM** -> 21030 | - -> 126.80 / 126.94 |

main fails in the first denoising step: `Tried to allocate 384.00 MiB ... 26.89 GiB is allocated by PyTorch`, capacity 31.36 GiB. `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` does not remove it: main fails the same way with 28.14 GiB allocated and 1.21 GiB reserved but unallocated. These runs do not separate a pure capacity shortage from a residual allocation limit. A per-stage probe on main confirms denoising is the request peak on this card (17653 / 20255 / 25467 MB for n=1/2/4, against 16311 MB for conditioning and 4850 / 8023 / 14371 MB for decode).

**RTX 4090 24 GB, cookbook multi-output recipe** (`--performance-mode manual --dit-layerwise-offload true --text-encoder-cpu-offload true`, FlashAttention). One timed request.

| config | main | here |
|---|---|---|
| CFG off, n=1 / 2 / 4 latency (s) | 25.35 / 48.55 / 96.33 | 25.35 / 48.01 / 94.35 |
| CFG 4, n=1 / 2 latency (s) | 49.85 / 96.20 | 49.82 / 95.69 |
| CFG 4, n=4 | **OOM** | 187.11 s |

Recorded peak allocated is 18650-18669 MB in every successful config on both sides. A per-stage probe on main shows why: the conditioning stage peaks at 18650 MB for every n, above denoising (4397 / 7000 / 12211 MB for n=1/2/4) and decode (4094 / 7267 / 13615 MB).

main's OOM is again in the first denoising step, with `16.70 GiB allocated ... 5.48 GiB reserved but unallocated` of 23.52 GiB. This one is an allocator-fragmentation failure, not a capacity limit: with `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` main completes the same request (189.63 s). This change avoids it under the default allocator by keeping the denoising footprint smaller. On the RTX 5090 that setting did not help, as noted above.

**RTX PRO 6000 96 GB, default flags** (everything resident, so the batched VAE decode is the peak without CFG). Two timed requests.

| config | peak allocated main -> here (MB) | peak reserved main -> here (MB) | latency main -> here (s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| CFG off, n=2 | 22002 -> 22002 | 31216 -> 28720 | 18.93 / 19.07 -> 18.77 / 18.84 |
| CFG off, n=4 | 28352 -> 28352 | 46510 -> 39470 | 37.97 / 38.25 -> 37.34 / 37.61 |
| CFG 4, n=2 | 25019 -> 22002 | 36402 -> 31410 | 37.53 / 37.77 -> 37.06 / 37.32 |
| CFG 4, n=4 | 34346 -> 28353 | 55746 -> 41776 | 75.24 / 75.45 -> 74.13 / 74.21 |

n=1 is unchanged everywhere. On this card the allocated peak only drops under CFG; without CFG the decode peak (about 3.17 GB per output) hides it. Decoding one sample at a time (#40493) removes that peak there: n=4 goes 28352 -> 19613 MB (CFG off) and 34346 -> 21677 MB (CFG 4) with both changes, versus 26115 / 34346 with #40493 alone.

In these samples end-to-end latency for n>1 was 0.5-2.1% lower with this change (two timed requests per config on RTX PRO 6000 and RTX 5090, one on RTX 4090; variants were run in a fixed order, not interleaved). Skipping the repeated prefills is the expected source, but prefill time was not measured separately.

issues.title: [diffusion] Honor --vae-slicing in the native decoding stage
issues.body:
## Motivation

`--vae-slicing` exists, but only the Diffusers backend honors it. The native `DecodingStage` never calls `enable_slicing()`, and `ParallelTiledVAE` (the base of the Qwen-Image 2.1, Wan and other native VAEs) has no slicing path, so the flag is a no-op there.

That matters for multi-output requests. On Qwen-Image 2.1 (`/v1/images/edits`, 1024x1024, 40 steps, RTX PRO 6000 96 GB, resident), per-stage peaks show the request peak is the batched VAE decode, growing about 3.17 GB per output:

| stage peak allocated (MB) | n=1 | n=2 | n=4 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| denoising | 18298 | 18712 | 19612 |
| decoding | 18829 | 22001 | 28349 |

(Per-stage numbers were taken with prefix KV sharing from #40489 applied; the decode figures equal main's request peaks below to within 3 MB.)

## Modifications

- `DecodingStage.decode`: when `pipeline_config.vae_slicing` is set, decode one sample per call and concatenate. This applies to every VAE decoded through `DecodingStage` and does not depend on each VAE's own slicing support. Pipelines with their own decode stage are not covered.
- Default stays off, so existing behavior is unchanged.

An earlier revision of this PR put the slicing in `ParallelTiledVAE` and called `enable_slicing()`. That silently did nothing on Wan's default path: `AutoencoderKLWan.decode` has no slicing check and, with the feature cache on (the default), calls its decoder directly. The current code was run on Qwen-Image 2.1 and once on Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B (n=2, 17 frames): without the flag `AutoencoderKLWan.decode` receives `z=(2, 16, 5, 60, 104)` on the feature-cache path and the decode stage peaks at 13609 MB; with it, `z=(1, ...)` twice and 7016 MB. Other models are covered by the unit test only. The measurements below were taken with that revision on Qwen-Image 2.1, where the per-sample computation is the same; one config was re-run with the current code and is pixel-identical to it, the rest were not re-run.

## Accuracy Tests

- The new unit test fails on main's stage (`[3] != [1, 1, 1]` decode batch sizes) and passes here; `test_decoding_stage_parallelism.py` passes in full (10 passed). pre-commit passes.
- Slicing is **not bit-exact** against batched decode in BF16. Versus main with the same request and seed: n=1 identical; n>1 has 5.1-7.1% of channel values differing, max abs diff 4-10 of 255, mean abs diff 0.051-0.071, PSNR 59.5-61.1 dB, 0.005-0.04% of values differing by more than 1. Sliced output is run-to-run identical. This is why it stays opt-in.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same protocol for every row: fresh `sglang serve` per config (`--vae-slicing true` where noted), 1 warm + 2 timed edit requests, seed 42, peaks from `perf_dump_path`. "both" adds #40489.

| config | variant | peak allocated (MB) | peak reserved (MB) | decode (ms) | latency (s) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| CFG off, n=1 | main | 18829 | 23404 | 434 | 9.60 / 9.62 |
| | slicing | 18829 | 23404 | 432 | 9.57 / 9.61 |
| CFG off, n=2 | main | 22002 | 31216 | 631 | 18.93 / 19.07 |
| | slicing | 20902 | 26616 | 635 | 18.91 / 19.00 |
| | both | 18839 | 24120 | 642 | 18.70 / 18.79 |
| CFG off, n=4 | main | 28352 | 46510 | 1001 | 37.97 / 38.25 |
| | slicing | 26115 | 32118 | 1221 | 37.80 / 38.04 |
| | both | 19613 | 25078 | 1223 | 37.21 / 37.51 |
| CFG 4, n=4 | main | 34346 | 55746 | - | 75.24 / 75.45 |
| | slicing | 34346 | 41354 | 1233 | 75.43 / 75.23 |
| | both | 21677 | 27384 | 1233 | 74.09 / 74.20 |

Reading: slicing alone moves the peak from decode to denoising (n=4: -2.2 GB allocated, -14 GB reserved) and does nothing for allocated peak under CFG, where denoising already dominates. With #40489 the n=4 peak is 0.8 GB above n=1. Decode costs +220 ms at n=4; end-to-end latency did not regress in these two samples per config.

Offload deployments, same protocol: RTX 5090 32 GB (default flags: `dit_cpu_offload`) and RTX 4090 24 GB (cookbook recipe: `--dit-layerwise-offload true --text-encoder-cpu-offload true`), n up to 4. There `--vae-slicing true` did not change recorded peak allocated in any config and did not resolve main's CFG n=4 OOM on its own, because decode is not the request peak: on the 4090 the conditioning stage peaks at 18650 MB for every n, against 4094 / 7267 / 13615 MB for decode at n=1/2/4. Peak reserved did drop in some configs (4090, CFG off n=4: 20490 -> 19332 MB; on top of #40489 at CFG n=4: 21990 -> 19340 MB on the 4090 and 25536 -> 23684 MB on the 5090). Latency showed no difference in these samples, and n>1 pixels differ as above (max abs diff 5-19).

Larger n on the same RTX 4090 recipe (CFG off, per-stage peak allocated from a temporary probe; the conditioning stage is 18634-18656 MB in every run):

| code | n | `--vae-slicing` | denoising (MB) | decode (MB) | result |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| main + this PR | 6 | off | 17426 | 19967 | ok, 143.03 s |
| main + this PR | 6 | on | 17426 | 4146 | ok, 142.85 s |
| main + this PR | 8 | off / on | - | - | OOM in the first denoising step |
| + #40489 | 6 | on | 6611 | 4146 | ok, 138.83 s |
| + #40489 | 8 | off | 7503 | - | OOM in decode |
| + #40489 | 8 | on | 7509 | 4164 | ok, 187.00 s |

Slicing holds decode at about 4.1 GB regardless of n. At n=6 it moves the request peak from decode back to the conditioning stage. At n=8 the request completes only with both changes: without slicing, decode asks for a single 9.00 GiB allocation on top of 16.69 GiB, which does not fit the 23.52 GiB card (also with `expandable_segments:True`); without #40489, denoising OOMs under both allocator settings. One more config, + #40489 at n=6 without slicing, OOMed in decode under the default allocator but completed with `expandable_segments:True` (decode 19954 MB), so it is not counted as evidence here. One timed request per config.

issues.title: [Perf] diffusion: fused gate/up + SwiGLU MLP on comfy_kitchen INT8 for Qwen-Image 2.1
issues.body:
## Motivation

On the comfy_kitchen INT8 backend, Qwen-Image 2.1's MLP ran three GEMMs plus a standalone SiLU-mul: `gate_layer`, `proj`, `silu(gate) * up` written to HBM in BF16, then `out`. ComfyUI runs the same checkpoint as one `[gate | up]` GEMM and a down-projection that applies the SwiGLU inside its quantizer (`int8_linear(..., input_act="swiglu")`).

## Modifications

- `convrot_int8_comfy_kitchen.py`: add `comfy_kitchen_swiglu_mlp`, which makes the two kitchen calls. The linear method's `apply` is unchanged.
- `qwen_image21.py`:
  - `pack_gate_up_weights()` runs from `post_load_weights` and from `_apply`, so packing survives `.to()` and CPU offload. It puts the `gate_layer`/`proj` INT8 weights and row scales into one storage each. This mirrors `pack_qkv_weights`: parameters keep their names and shapes, and no reference to the shared storage is kept.
  - `packed_gate_up()` re-derives the stacked views on every forward.
  - LoRA wrappers, layerwise-offload placeholders, TP > 1, torch.compile and the JIT backend keep the separate projections.

## Accuracy Tests

- The stacked GEMM computes the same per-column arithmetic as the two separate projections.
- The fused quantizer keeps `silu(gate) * up` in FP32 instead of rounding it to BF16 first, so outputs are **not bitwise** the previous path.
  - Against an FP32 reference, relative L2 error is 1.33% for the fused path vs 1.35% for eager at (2048, 3072→1024), and 1.44% vs 1.46% at (4096, 12288→4096).
  - It is the same call ComfyUI makes for this model.
- New unit test (`test_convrot_int8_backends.py`) checks:
  - the fused error vs FP32 is no worse than eager's;
  - re-packing after a CPU round trip;
  - the fallback is bitwise the eager path once the shared storage is gone.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen-Image 2.1 INT8 checkpoint, comfy_kitchen backend, SGLD ComfyUI workflow, 8 steps × 3 seeds. Steady model-time gain:

| GPU | CFG 1 | CFG 4 |
|---|---:|---:|
| RTX 4090 | +4.75% | +4.46% |
| RTX 5090 | +4.44% | +4.16% |
| H200 (kitchen forced) | +3.17% | +2.46% |

H200, B200 and RTX 5090 default to the JIT backend, where this path is inactive. RTX 4090 (sm89) always uses comfy_kitchen.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
